questions.q: Which of the following best defines 'Commerce' as studied in secondary school Business subjects?
o: The process of turning raw materials into finished goods in a factory
The system by which government controls the prices of goods
The act of growing crops and rearing animals for sale
The branch of economic activity concerned with buying and selling of goods and services, and all activities that help make this exchange possible
questions.e: Commerce covers trade (buying and selling) plus all the aids to trade (like banking, transport, insurance) that make exchange of goods and services possible. Manufacturing, farming and price control are not commerce.
questions.p: Commerce na di branch of economic activity wey dey cover buying and selling, plus all di helpers like bank, transport, insurance wey dey make exchange possible. To turn raw material to goods na manufacturing, farming na agriculture, price control na government work, no be commerce.

questions.q: Chidi's main job is teaching mathematics in a secondary school in Enugu. Under the classification of occupations, his job falls under which category?
o: Direct service occupation
Extractive occupation
Construction occupation
Manufacturing occupation
questions.e: Teaching is a personal service rendered directly to people, so it is classified as a direct service, which is part of indirect occupations alongside commerce. It is not extractive, manufacturing, or construction, because those involve producing physical goods.
questions.p: Teaching na personal service wey person dey give to pipo direct, so dem dey call am direct service, wey dey under indirect occupation together with commerce. E no be extractive, manufacturing or construction because dem ones dey produce physical goods.

questions.q: Which of the following activities is an example of an 'aid to trade' within the scope of Commerce?
o: Weaving of cloth in a textile factory
Farming of cassava in Benue State
Insurance of goods against fire and theft
Mining of tin in Jos
questions.e: Insurance helps reduce the risk involved in trade, making it an aid to trade under commerce. Farming, mining and weaving are direct occupations (extractive and manufacturing), not aids to trade.
questions.p: Insurance dey help reduce di risk wey dey inside trade, so e be aid to trade under commerce. Farming, mining and weaving na direct occupation (extractive and manufacturing), dem no be aid to trade.

questions.q: The scope of Commerce includes all of the following EXCEPT one. Identify the exception.
o: Transport and communication
Manufacturing of finished goods in a factory
Trade (wholesale and retail)
Banking and insurance
questions.e: Commerce covers trade and the aids to trade such as banking, insurance, transport and communication. Manufacturing is a direct (industrial) occupation concerned with production, so it is outside the scope of commerce.
questions.p: Commerce dey cover trade and di aids to trade like banking, insurance, transport and communication. Manufacturing na direct (industrial) occupation wey dey concern production, so e no dey inside scope of commerce.

questions.q: Mrs. Balogun buys yams from farmers in Niger State, uses a transport company to move them to Lagos, insures them against damage on the road, and finally sells them in her market stall. Which statement correctly explains the scope of her full business activity?
o: Only the transport and insurance count as commerce; buying and selling are classified as industry
The whole process is commerce, since it combines trade (buying and selling) with aids to trade (transport and insurance)
Only the buying and selling count as commerce; the transport and insurance have nothing to do with commerce
The whole process is industry, because goods were physically moved from one place to another
questions.e: Commerce is made up of trade (buying and selling) plus the aids to trade (like transport and insurance) that remove barriers of place and risk. Mrs. Balogun's whole process fits this definition, so it is all commerce, not industry.
questions.p: Commerce na trade (buying and selling) plus di aids to trade (like transport and insurance) wey dey remove barrier of place and risk. Wetin Mrs. Balogun do na full commerce, e no be industry.

questions.q: Adaeze catches fish from the Lagos lagoon herself and sells the fish directly to buyers at the waterside, without passing through any middleman. Which two occupations best describe her activities?
o: Manufacturing and direct service
Extractive occupation and commerce
Construction and aids to trade
Direct service only, since she does both jobs herself
questions.e: Catching fish from nature is an extractive occupation, while selling the fish to buyers is trade, which is part of commerce. Her activity is not manufacturing, construction, or a direct service alone, since she is both extracting and trading goods.
questions.p: To catch fish from nature na extractive occupation, and to sell di fish na trade, wey be part of commerce. E no be manufacturing, construction or direct service alone, because she dey both extract and trade goods.

questions.q: Commerce is sometimes described as a 'bridge' that links producers to final consumers. This description mainly refers to the way commerce helps to remove barriers such as:
o: Barriers of climate that affect farming output
Barriers created by government taxation policies alone
Barriers of person, place, time, and risk that separate producers from consumers
Barriers of language only between buyers and sellers
questions.e: Commerce bridges the gap between producers and consumers by solving problems of place (through transport), person (through trade/middlemen), time (through warehousing), and risk (through insurance). The other options are too narrow or unrelated to this core idea.
questions.p: Commerce dey connect producer and consumer by solving problem of place (through transport), person (through trade/middlemen), time (through warehouse), and risk (through insurance). Di oda options too small or no concern dis main point.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT regarded as one of the four basic factors of production in Commerce?
o: Labour
Land
Capital
Money
questions.e: The four factors of production are land, labour, capital and entrepreneur. Money is not a factor on its own; it is only a tool used to acquire capital goods for production.
questions.p: The four main factors of production na land, labour, capital and entrepreneur. Money no be factor by itself, na just tool wey dem dey use buy capital goods.

questions.q: Production that involves the extraction or gathering of raw materials directly from nature, such as mining, fishing, and crop farming, is classified as ______ production.
o: Primary
Secondary
Tertiary
Quaternary
questions.e: Primary production deals with the direct extraction of natural resources like minerals, fish, and crops from land and water. Secondary production processes these raw materials, while tertiary production provides services.
questions.p: Primary production na when dem comot raw materials straight from nature, like mining, fishing and farming. Secondary na when dem process the raw materials, tertiary na services.

questions.q: Chidinma owns a small factory in Aba where raw cassava tubers are processed into garri for sale to retailers. This activity is best classified as ______ production.
o: Extractive
Primary
Secondary
Tertiary
questions.e: Secondary production involves transforming raw materials like cassava into finished or semi-finished goods such as garri through manufacturing or processing. It happens after primary production supplies the raw cassava.
questions.p: Secondary production na when dem change raw material (cassava) to finished product (garri) through processing. Na after primary production don bring the raw cassava.

questions.q: What is the reward paid to a person who supplies capital for use in production?
o: Interest
Wage
Profit
Rent
questions.e: Interest is the payment made to the owner of capital for its use in production. Rent goes to land, wage goes to labour, and profit goes to the entrepreneur.
questions.p: Interest na the payment wey dem dey give owner of capital for how im capital help production. Rent na for land, wage na for labour, profit na for entrepreneur.

questions.q: Which factor of production is primarily responsible for taking business risks, organizing the other factors, and making key managerial decisions in a firm?
o: Capital
Labour
Land
Entrepreneur
questions.e: The entrepreneur combines land, labour and capital, bears the risk of production, and makes major business decisions in hope of earning profit. The other three factors cannot organize themselves without the entrepreneur.
questions.p: Entrepreneur na im dey combine land, labour and capital, e dey carry risk, e dey make important business decisions so im fit make profit. Without entrepreneur, the other factors no fit organize themselves.

questions.q: Mallam Sule has spent 15 years as a traditional blacksmith making farm hoes and cutlasses. When demand for his tools dropped sharply because farmers now prefer imported tractors, he could not easily switch to become a tractor mechanic without undergoing years of fresh training. This situation best illustrates which characteristic of labour as a factor of production?
o: Division of labour
Occupational immobility of labour
Specialization of labour
Geographical immobility of labour
questions.e: Occupational immobility of labour occurs when a worker cannot easily move from one type of job to another because of lack of the required skills or training. Mallam Sule cannot shift from blacksmithing to mechanics without retraining, which shows this characteristic clearly.
questions.p: Occupational immobility of labour na when worker no fit easily change im job to another type of work because im no get the skill or training for the new work. Mallam Sule no fit just become mechanic without fresh training, so na occupational immobility be dat.

questions.q: In Commerce, the factor of production known as 'land' refers to ______.
o: only the soil used for crop farming
all free gifts of nature used in production, such as soil, water, forests and minerals
money invested in purchasing landed property
buildings and structures erected by man on a site
questions.e: In Commerce and Economics, land covers all natural resources provided by nature and used in production, not just soil. This includes water bodies, forests, minerals, climate, and sunlight.
questions.p: For Commerce, land no mean soil alone, e cover all natural resources wey nature give for production use, like water, forest, minerals and climate.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of tertiary production?
o: Banking services offered by a commercial bank
Tin mining in Jos
Fishing along the coast of Lagos
Baking of bread in a bakery
questions.e: Tertiary production involves the provision of services such as banking, transport, and insurance that support primary and secondary production. Mining and fishing are examples of primary production, while baking is secondary production.
questions.p: Tertiary production na about services like banking, transport and insurance wey dey support primary and secondary production. Mining and fishing na primary, baking na secondary.

questions.q: What does the term 'home trade' mean in Commerce?
o: Trade carried out only by government agencies
Exchange of goods for goods without the use of money
Buying and selling of goods between two or more countries
Buying and selling of goods within the boundaries of one country
questions.e: Home trade is trade that takes place within the borders of a single country, as opposed to foreign trade which involves more than one country. Example is a trader in Kano selling to a buyer in Lagos.
questions.p: Home trade na trade wey dey happen inside one kontri only. E different from foreign trade wey dey cross kontri border. E.g trader for Kano wey dey sell to buyer for Lagos.

questions.q: Home trade is usually divided into two main branches. Which pair correctly names these branches?
o: Visible trade and invisible trade
Entrepot trade and bilateral trade
Retail trade and wholesale trade
Import trade and export trade
questions.e: Within a country, home trade is split into wholesale trade (buying and selling in large quantities) and retail trade (buying and selling in small quantities to final consumers).
questions.p: Home trade get two main parts: wholesale trade (dem dey buy and sell plenty-plenty) and retail trade (dem dey sell small-small to final consumer).

questions.q: Which of the following best describes wholesale trade?
o: Buying goods in bulk from producers and selling in smaller quantities to retailers
Buying goods from retailers in order to resell them to producers
Selling directly to final consumers in very small units
Exchanging goods between two trading countries
questions.e: A wholesaler buys goods in large quantities directly (or almost directly) from producers at a lower price, then sells in smaller quantities to retailers, acting as a middleman between producer and retailer.
questions.p: Wholesaler dey buy plenty goods from producer cheap-cheap, then e go sell small-small quantity give retailer. E be like middle man between producer and retailer.

questions.q: Mrs Adaeze, a retailer in Onitsha market, prefers to buy her stock from a wholesaler instead of directly from the manufacturer. One key service the wholesaler provides her is that he...
o: Manufactures special goods only for her shop
Fixes the final retail price of all goods for her
Collects value added tax on her behalf for government
Breaks bulk goods into smaller units that she can afford and store
questions.e: A major function of the wholesaler is breaking bulk, that is, dividing large quantities bought from producers into smaller units that small retailers like Mrs Adaeze can afford to buy and have space to store.
questions.p: Wholesaler dey break bulk, meaning e go divide the plenty goods wey e buy from producer into small-small units wey retailer fit buy and get space to keep.

questions.q: A particular type of trader has no fixed shop. He moves from one village or street to another, carrying goods such as wristwatches and clothes to sell directly to customers wherever he finds them. This type of trader is called a/an...
o: Department store owner
Chain store operator
Itinerant trader
Cooperative retailer
questions.e: An itinerant trader, also called a hawker or peddler, has no permanent business premises. He moves about from place to place selling his goods, which is common in many Nigerian towns and markets.
questions.p: Itinerant trader (hawker) no get fixed shop. E dey carry im goods waka from place to place to sell am wherever e see customer, common for many Nigerian towns.

questions.q: Which statement correctly describes the main function of a retailer in the chain of distribution?
o: The retailer buys goods only from foreign producers
The retailer breaks bulk and sells goods in small quantities to final consumers
The retailer manufactures raw materials into finished goods
The retailer controls the price fixed by government for all goods
questions.e: The retailer is the last link between the wholesaler (or producer) and the final consumer. His main job is to break bulk further and sell goods in small, convenient quantities, such as selling a single tin of milk instead of a full carton.
questions.p: Retailer na the last person before final consumer. Im main work na to break the goods wey e buy small-small so e fit sell am like one tin milk instead of full carton.

questions.q: Chidi, a retailer, buys a carton of provisions from a wholesaler for ₦9,000. He divides the carton into 20 equal units to sell. If Chidi wants to make a total profit of ₦2,000 on the whole carton, at what price must he sell each unit?
questions.e: Total amount Chidi needs from selling all units = cost + profit = 9000 + 2000 = 11000. Dividing this by the 20 units gives 11000/20 = 550 naira per unit.
questions.p: The total money wey Chidi suppose collect = cost add profit = 9000 + 2000 = 11000 naira. If you divide 11000 by the 20 units, e go be 550 naira for each unit.

questions.q: A wholesaler renders several useful services to the producer who supplies him goods. Which of the following is NOT one of such services?
o: Serving as a ready outlet for goods produced in large quantities
Relieving the producer of the need to keep large stocks by buying in bulk
Giving the producer feedback and information about market demand
Granting direct control over retail prices to the final consumers
questions.e: Wholesalers help producers by buying in bulk, storing goods, providing market feedback and acting as an outlet for mass production. However, giving final consumers direct control over retail prices is not a service a wholesaler renders to a producer; it is not even a real trade function.
questions.p: Wholesaler dey help producer by buying plenty goods, keeping stock, and giving market information. But to give final consumer power to control retail price no be wetin wholesaler dey do for producer; e no even dey happen for real trade.

questions.q: Which document serves as evidence of a contract of carriage of goods by sea, acts as a receipt for the goods shipped, and also serves as a document of title to the goods?
o: Bill of Lading
Bill of Sight
Certificate of Origin
Bill of Exchange
questions.e: A Bill of Lading is issued by the shipping company to the exporter. It proves that goods have been loaded on board a ship and can be used to transfer ownership of the goods.
questions.p: Bill of Lading na di paper wey shipping company give di exporter wen dem don load di goods for ship. E dey show say di goods dey for ship and e fit transfer ownership of di goods.

questions.q: In foreign trade, which document states the country in which goods being exported were actually manufactured or produced?
o: Import Licence
Consular Invoice
Certificate of Origin
Letter of Credit
questions.e: A Certificate of Origin shows the country where goods were manufactured. It is important for customs duty purposes and for checking trade agreements between countries.
questions.p: Certificate of Origin na di paper wey show di kontri wey dem produce di goods. Customs dey use am to check duty and trade agreement between kontris.

questions.q: Chinwe, an importer in Lagos, wants her bank to guarantee payment to her overseas supplier once the supplier presents shipping documents proving goods have been sent as agreed. Which document should her bank issue to the supplier?
o: Charter Party
Bill of Lading
Letter of Credit
Certificate of Origin
questions.e: A Letter of Credit is a guarantee from the importer's bank to pay the exporter once agreed conditions, such as submission of correct shipping documents, are met. It reduces the risk of non-payment in foreign trade.
questions.p: Letter of Credit na guarantee wey di importer bank dey give say dem go pay di exporter once di correct documents don show. E dey reduce risk say exporter no go collect money.

questions.q: If the total value of a country's visible imports is less than the total value of its visible exports within a given year, this situation is best described as a
o: balance of payments deficit
favourable balance of trade
balance of payments surplus
unfavourable balance of trade
questions.e: When visible exports exceed visible imports, the country has earned more from selling goods abroad than it spent on buying them, which is called a favourable balance of trade.
questions.p: When di goods wey kontri sell abroad pass wetin e buy from abroad, dem dey call am favourable balance of trade because di kontri don make surplus for di trade.

questions.q: Which of the following items is classified as an invisible item in a country's balance of payments account?
o: Export of crude oil
Import of machinery
Export of cocoa
Income earned from tourism services
questions.e: Invisible items are services, not physical goods, such as tourism, insurance, banking and shipping services. Crude oil, machinery and cocoa are all tangible goods, so they are visible trade items.
questions.p: Invisible items na services, no be real goods wey you fit touch, like tourism, insurance and shipping. Crude oil, machinery and cocoa na physical goods, so na visible trade.

questions.q: A JAMB candidate was asked to distinguish between balance of trade and balance of payments. Which statement correctly explains the difference?
o: Balance of trade covers only visible items while balance of payments covers both visible and invisible items
Balance of trade covers invisible items while balance of payments covers only visible items
Balance of trade and balance of payments mean exactly the same thing
Balance of trade is wider in scope than balance of payments
questions.e: Balance of trade records only visible items, that is, physical goods exported and imported. Balance of payments is broader because it records both visible items and invisible items like services, interest, and capital movements.
questions.p: Balance of trade na only visible items, wey be physical goods wey dem export and import. Balance of payments wide pass am because e include both visible and invisible items like services and capital movement.

questions.q: Which document does a seller send to a buyer, showing the quantity, description and price of goods supplied, and the total amount the buyer owes?
o: Invoice
Receipt
Debit note
Credit note
questions.e: An invoice is the bill of sale a seller gives to a buyer, stating the goods supplied and the amount payable. It is different from a receipt, which only proves that payment has been made.
questions.p: Invoice na di paper wey seller give buyer, e show di goods wey dem supply and di money wey buyer go pay. E no be receipt, because receipt na wetin dem give after money don already pay.

questions.q: Trade discount is best described as a reduction which a
o: bank gives a customer for operating a current account
seller gives a buyer for paying cash promptly
manufacturer or wholesaler gives off the list price to encourage retailers to buy in bulk
government gives a company for exporting goods
questions.e: Trade discount is a percentage reduction off the catalogue (list) price given by a manufacturer or wholesaler to a trade buyer, usually for buying in large quantities; it is not recorded separately in the books. Cash discount, on the other hand, is for prompt payment.
questions.p: Trade discount na percentage wey manufacturer or wholesaler dey remove from list price to encourage buyer wey buy plenty goods. E no be di one wey dem give for fast payment — that one na cash discount.

questions.q: A wholesaler's list price for a batch of exercise books is ₦50,000. He grants Mr. Okafor, a retailer, a trade discount of 15% for buying in bulk. What is the amount of trade discount allowed?
questions.e: Trade discount = 15% of ₦50,000 = 0.15 x 50,000 = ₦7,500. This is the amount deducted from the list price before Mr. Okafor pays.
questions.p: Trade discount = 15% of ₦50,000 = 0.15 x 50,000 = ₦7,500. Na dis amount dem go remove from di list price before Okafor go pay.

questions.q: Chidinma's invoice for goods bought shows a price of ₦40,000. The supplier offers a 5% cash discount if payment is made within 14 days. If Chidinma pays within the 14 days, how much will she actually pay?
questions.e: Cash discount = 5% of ₦40,000 = ₦2,000. Amount payable = 40,000 - 2,000 = ₦38,000. This discount rewards Chidinma for paying promptly.
questions.p: Cash discount = 5% of ₦40,000 = ₦2,000. Wetin she go pay = 40,000 - 2,000 = ₦38,000. Na reward for fast payment.

questions.q: In international trade documentation, the price quotation 'CIF' means that the quoted price covers which combination of costs?
o: Credit, Insurance and Finance
Cost, Insurance and Freight
Cost, Import and Freight
Cost, Investment and Freight
questions.e: CIF stands for Cost, Insurance and Freight. It means the seller's quoted price already includes the cost of the goods, insurance during shipment, and freight (transport) charges up to the destination port.
questions.p: CIF mean Cost, Insurance and Freight. E mean say di price wey seller quote don already cover di goods cost, insurance wey dem use for di journey, and freight (transport) charge reach di destination port.

questions.q: A Nigerian importer agrees to buy machinery on 'FOB' terms from a foreign supplier. Under this term, the seller's responsibility for the goods ends as soon as the goods
o: arrive at the buyer's warehouse in Nigeria
are insured by the buyer
pass through customs in Nigeria
are loaded on board the ship at the port of shipment
questions.e: FOB means Free On Board. The seller's duty and cost responsibility end once the goods are loaded onto the ship at the port of shipment; after that, the buyer bears the freight, insurance and risk.
questions.p: FOB mean Free On Board. Seller responsibility end immediately dem load di goods for inside ship for di port wey dem dey ship from; after dat one, na buyer go carry freight, insurance and risk.

questions.q: Mrs. Bello wants to buy goods listed at ₦100,000 from a wholesaler who allows a 10% trade discount, plus a further 5% cash discount for payment within 30 days. If Mrs. Bello pays within 30 days, how much will she pay in total?
questions.e: First apply trade discount: 100,000 x (1 - 0.10) = ₦90,000. Then apply cash discount on this new amount: 90,000 x (1 - 0.05) = ₦85,500. Trade discount is deducted first, then cash discount is calculated on the reduced price.
questions.p: First remove trade discount: 100,000 x (1 - 0.10) = ₦90,000. Den remove cash discount from dat new amount: 90,000 x (1 - 0.05) = ₦85,500. Trade discount dey come first, cash discount go follow am on top di new price.

questions.q: Adaeze received an invoice for goods bought from a supplier, but on delivery she discovered that goods worth ₦6,000 were damaged and returned them. Which document will the supplier issue to Adaeze to reduce the amount she owes?
o: Receipt
Invoice
Credit note
Debit note
questions.e: A credit note is issued by a seller to a buyer when goods are returned or an overcharge is corrected; it reduces the amount the buyer owes. A debit note, in contrast, is used to increase the amount owed, such as for undercharged goods.
questions.p: Credit note na wetin seller go give buyer when buyer return goods or when dem over-charge am; e go reduce wetin buyer owe. Debit note na di opposite, na im dem dey use increase wetin person owe, like when dem under-charge goods.

questions.q: Which of the following best defines advertising as used in Commerce?
o: A personal visit by a salesman to a customer's home
A paid, non-personal form of communication used to promote goods, services or ideas
A reduction in the price of goods during festive seasons
A free gift given to a customer who buys a product
questions.e: Advertising is a paid, non-personal message passed through media like television, radio or newspapers to inform and persuade buyers. It is not a personal, face-to-face activity like personal selling.
questions.p: Advertising na message wey company pay money for, wey no be face-to-face, dem dey use am tell people about goods or service. E no be like when salesman come your house talk to you one-on-one.

questions.q: Which of these is an example of sales promotion rather than advertising?
o: A jingle played on radio about a soft drink
A full-page advert in a national newspaper
A 'buy two, get one free' offer on bags of rice for one week
A billboard poster along a major expressway
questions.e: Sales promotion involves short-term incentives like 'buy two, get one free' to boost immediate sales. Radio jingles, billboards and newspaper adverts are forms of advertising, not sales promotion.
questions.p: Sales promotion na short-term offer like 'buy two, collect one free' wey dey push people to buy quick-quick. Radio jingle, billboard and newspaper advert na advertising, no be sales promotion.

questions.q: A major objective of advertising a new brand of toothpaste in Nigeria would be to:
o: Create awareness and persuade consumers to try the new brand
Reduce the company's production cost immediately
Replace the need for product packaging
Eliminate the role of middlemen in distribution
questions.e: Advertising mainly aims to inform people about a product and persuade them to buy it, especially when it is newly introduced. It does not directly reduce production cost, remove packaging, or eliminate middlemen.
questions.p: The main reason to advertise new toothpaste na to make people know say the product dey and convince dem make dem try am. E no be to reduce production cost, remove packaging, or comot middlemen.

questions.q: Mama Chidi owns a provision store in a rural community where most customers cannot read. Which advertising medium would reach her customers most effectively?
o: Billboard with only written text along the expressway
Newspaper advert in a national daily
Magazine advert placed in a glossy publication
Radio jingle in the local language
questions.e: Radio does not require literacy and can reach people in their local language, making it ideal for rural, mostly non-literate audiences. Newspapers, billboards with text, and magazines require the ability to read.
questions.p: Radio no need person to sabi read, e dey use local language wey everybody for village go understand. Newspaper, billboard wit only writing, and magazine need say person sabi read before e go understand.

questions.q: Which of the following is a key difference between advertising and personal selling?
o: Personal selling cannot be used to promote industrial goods
Advertising is a mass, impersonal communication while personal selling is direct and face-to-face
Advertising involves direct face-to-face contact while personal selling does not
Advertising is always more expensive per customer reached than personal selling
questions.e: Advertising reaches a large, impersonal audience through media, while personal selling involves a salesperson dealing directly with a customer. This direct human contact allows personal selling to answer specific customer questions immediately.
questions.p: Advertising na mass message wey reach plenty people same time without person-to-person contact, but personal selling na direct wia salesman dey meet customer face-to-face. Na the face-to-face wey be the main difference.

questions.q: A beverage company gives out free sachets of a new malt drink to shoppers at a supermarket to encourage them to try it. This activity is best described as:
o: Publicity
Institutional advertising
Sales promotion
Personal selling
questions.e: Giving free samples to encourage trial of a product is a classic short-term sales promotion technique. It is not publicity (which is unpaid media coverage) or personal selling (which involves persuasion through conversation).
questions.p: To give people free sample make dem try new product na sales promotion wey dey short-term. E no be publicity (wey be free media coverage) or personal selling (wey be persuade person for mouth-to-mouth talk).

questions.q: Which of the following is a common criticism against advertising as a method of sales promotion?
o: It can mislead consumers through exaggerated claims about a product
It guarantees that every advertised product will sell well
It completely removes the need for product quality
It always makes products permanently cheaper for consumers
questions.e: A major criticism of advertising is that some adverts exaggerate or mislead consumers about what a product can really do. Advertising does not guarantee sales, lower prices, or remove the need for actual product quality.
questions.p: One big criticism against advertising na say sometimes e dey exaggerate or deceive people about wetin the product fit do. Advertising no dey guarantee sale, e no dey make price permanently cheap, and e no dey remove need for quality.

questions.q: A soap manufacturer notices that despite heavy television advertising, sales have not increased because retailers are not stocking enough units in shops. Which combined strategy would most likely solve this problem?
o: Reduce the quality of the soap to cut production cost
Offer trade discounts and bonus packs to retailers alongside the advertising
Increase television advertising spending without changing anything else
Stop advertising completely and rely only on word of mouth
questions.e: The problem is that retailers lack incentive to stock the product, so advertising alone (which targets final consumers) cannot fix it. Trade sales promotion tools like discounts and bonus packs directly motivate retailers to stock more units.
questions.p: The main wahala na say retailers no get enough motivation to stock the soap, so just dey advertise to consumers no go solve am. If dem give retailers discount and bonus packs, e go push dem to stock more, and that one go work with the advertising.

questions.q: Which of the following banks is the only one authorized by law to issue legal tender currency notes and coins in Nigeria?
o: Nigerian Export-Import Bank
Bank of Industry
First Bank of Nigeria
Central Bank of Nigeria
questions.e: The Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) has the sole legal right to print and issue Nigeria's currency. Other banks such as First Bank only accept deposits and lend money; they cannot print currency.
questions.p: Na only Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) get permission by law to print and bring out Naira notes and coins. Other banks like First Bank just dey collect money and give loan, dem no fit print money.

questions.q: A cheque has two parallel lines drawn across its face with the words 'Not Negotiable' written between the lines. What type of cheque is this?
o: Bearer cheque
Stale cheque
Crossed cheque
Open cheque
questions.e: Drawing two parallel lines across a cheque is called crossing, and it means the cheque must be paid only into a bank account, not cashed over the counter. This makes the cheque safer against theft.
questions.p: When you draw two lines for cheque face like that, dem dey call am crossed cheque. E mean say the money must enter bank account, dem no fit cash am for counter. E dey make the cheque safe from thief.

questions.q: Which of the following activities is NOT normally carried out by the Central Bank of Nigeria?
o: Acting as lender of last resort to commercial banks
Accepting savings deposits from ordinary members of the public
Acting as banker to the Federal Government
Issuing and controlling the national currency
questions.e: The CBN deals mainly with the government and commercial banks, not with individual members of the public. Accepting personal savings is the work of commercial banks like GTBank or Zenith Bank, not the CBN.
questions.p: CBN dey work with government and the commercial banks, e no dey open account for ordinary person. To collect person savings na work for commercial bank like GTBank or Zenith Bank, no be CBN work.

questions.q: Mr Okafor wrote a cheque of ₦50,000 to Mrs Bello, but when she took it to the bank, the bank refused to pay because Mr Okafor's account had only ₦10,000. What type of cheque is this?
o: Crossed cheque
Stale cheque
Post-dated cheque
Dishonoured cheque
questions.e: A cheque that a bank refuses to pay because the drawer's account lacks sufficient funds is called a dishonoured cheque. It has nothing to do with crossing, age, or a future date on the cheque.
questions.p: When bank refuse to pay cheque because the person wey write am no get enough money for im account, dem dey call am dishonoured cheque. E no concern crossing, how old the cheque be, or any future date for am.

questions.q: A bank that specializes in giving medium and long-term loans mainly for industrial and agricultural projects, instead of focusing on short-term deposits from the general public, is best classified as a ______.
o: development bank
savings bank
commercial bank
merchant bank
questions.e: Development banks, such as the Bank of Industry, exist specifically to finance long-term industrial and agricultural development, unlike commercial banks which focus on everyday deposits and short-term loans. Merchant banks mainly serve large businesses with corporate finance, not project-based long-term loans for development.
questions.p: Development bank like Bank of Industry na im dey give long-term loan for industry and farming matter. Commercial bank dey focus on everyday saving and short loan, while merchant bank dey handle big company money matter, no be long-term development loan.

questions.q: Which of the following is a direct service that commercial banks provide to their customers?
o: Safekeeping of customers' valuables in strong rooms
Printing of the national currency
Fixing the national minimum wage
Collection of import duties on behalf of government
questions.e: Commercial banks offer safe-keeping of valuables such as jewellery and documents in their strong rooms or safe deposit boxes as a customer service. Printing currency, fixing wages, and collecting duties are government or CBN functions, not commercial bank services.
questions.p: Commercial bank dey keep people valuable things like jewelry and important papers safe inside dia strong room, na one of dia service be dat. To print money, fix minimum wage, or collect duty na government or CBN work, no be commercial bank own.

questions.q: The Central Bank of Nigeria is often described as the 'lender of last resort' to commercial banks. This mainly means that the CBN lends money to a commercial bank, when the bank cannot get funds anywhere else, in order to ______.
o: increase the commercial bank's yearly profit
encourage more foreign investors to open accounts
prevent the collapse of the banking system
reduce the amount government spends yearly
questions.e: If a commercial bank cannot meet its obligations and no one else will lend to it, its failure could cause panic and spread to other banks. The CBN steps in as the final source of funds to keep that bank, and the whole banking system, stable and trusted.
questions.p: If commercial bank no fit pay wetin e owe and nobody wan lend am money again, e fit cause wahala wey go spread go other banks. CBN go come lend the bank money as last option so that the whole banking system no go scatter.

questions.q: A cheque was issued six months ago but has still not been presented to the bank for payment. The bank is now likely to refuse payment because the cheque has become a ______.
o: open cheque
blank cheque
crossed cheque
stale cheque
questions.e: A cheque that has not been presented for payment within a reasonable time, usually six months, is called a stale cheque, and banks normally refuse to honour it. Crossed, open, and blank cheques describe other features of a cheque, not its age.
questions.p: Cheque wey don tey reach like six months wey nobody bring am go bank, dem dey call am stale cheque, and bank no go gree pay am again. Crossed, open, and blank cheque na different matter entirely, e no concern how old the cheque be.

questions.q: In the history of trade, before money was invented, people exchanged goods directly for other goods without using any medium of exchange. What is this system of exchange called?
o: Commodity exchange
Trade by barter
Hire purchase
Deferred payment
questions.e: Trade by barter is the direct exchange of goods for goods without using money. It was the earliest method of trade before money was invented. The other options involve money or credit arrangements, which came after barter.
questions.p: Trade by barter na when person dey swap im goods for another goods, no money dey involve. Na the first kind trade before money come. The other options need money or credit wey come later.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the four main functions of money as studied in Commerce?
o: Medium of exchange
Store of value
Means of production
Standard for deferred payment
questions.e: The four main functions of money are medium of exchange, measure of value (unit of account), store of value, and standard for deferred payment. Means of production refers to land, labour and capital used to produce goods, which is not a function of money.
questions.p: Money get only four main functions: medium of exchange, unit of account, store of value, and standard for deferred payment. Means of production na land, labour and capital wey dem dey use produce goods, e no be money function.

questions.q: One of the major problems of trade by barter is that a person who wants to exchange his goods must find another person who has what he wants and also wants what he is offering at the same time. What is this problem called?
o: Lack of unit of account
Lack of portability
Lack of store of value
Lack of double coincidence of wants
questions.e: Under barter, trade can only happen when two people's needs match exactly at the same time; this is called lack of double coincidence of wants. Money solved this by acting as a universally accepted medium of exchange.
questions.p: For barter, trade fit only happen if the two people wey dey exchange goods need exactly wetin each other get at the same time; dem dey call am lack of double coincidence of wants. Money solve dis wahala because everybody dey accept am.

questions.q: A ₦1000 note can be exchanged for five ₦200 notes or ten ₦100 notes without any loss in value. Which quality of money does this situation illustrate?
o: Durability
Divisibility
Acceptability
Scarcity
questions.e: Divisibility means money can be broken into smaller units of lower value without losing its total worth. The example of ₦1000 being exchanged for smaller notes of equal total value shows this quality clearly.
questions.p: Divisibility mean say money fit break into smaller units wey no go lose value. The example of ₦1000 wey you fit change to smaller notes wey still equal am show dis quality well well.

questions.q: Alhaji Musa owns a cow worth ₦150,000 and wants to buy a bag of rice worth ₦30,000 from Mama Nkechi. Under trade by barter, Alhaji Musa cannot give out just a part of the cow to Mama Nkechi without killing the whole animal. This situation illustrates which problem of trade by barter?
o: Problem of indivisibility of goods
Lack of standard for deferred payment
Lack of a common measure of value
Lack of double coincidence of wants
questions.e: Some goods like a live cow cannot be broken into smaller parts to match a lower value without destroying them; this is the problem of indivisibility. Money solves this because it can be divided into smaller denominations.
questions.p: Some goods like live cow no fit break into small-small parts for lower value without you kill am; na dis dem dey call indivisibility problem. Money solve am because you fit break am into smaller notes or coins.

questions.q: Considering the historical evolution of money from trade by barter to modern electronic money, which stage came immediately before the widespread use of paper money (banknotes) in most economies?
o: Trade by barter
Electronic money/plastic money
Metallic money
Commodity money
questions.e: The generally accepted order of evolution is: trade by barter, commodity money, metallic money (coins made of gold, silver, etc.), paper money, and finally electronic/plastic money. Metallic money therefore directly preceded paper money.
questions.p: The order wey money develop be: trade by barter, commodity money, metallic money (coins wey dem make from gold, silver), paper money, then electronic/plastic money. So metallic money na im come before paper money.

questions.q: Which quality of money makes it possible for a trader to carry ₦50,000 in his pocket to the market instead of carrying bags of grains of equivalent value?
o: Scarcity
Portability
Durability
Acceptability
questions.e: Portability means money is light and easy to carry from one place to another, unlike bulky goods such as bags of grains. This makes trade faster and more convenient than carrying heavy goods for exchange.
questions.p: Portability mean say money dey light and e dey easy to carry from one place go another, unlike bags of grains wey heavy. Dis one make trade fast and easy pass when you go carry heavy goods.

questions.q: Insurance can best be described as a system in which:
o: a type of savings account offered only by commercial banks
a method of eliminating all risks associated with business operations
a government scheme that guarantees profit to every business
an arrangement in which individuals or firms pool funds (premiums) to compensate members who suffer specified losses
questions.e: Insurance is a risk-sharing arrangement where many people pay small amounts (premiums) into a common fund, and those who suffer a covered loss are compensated from the fund. It does not eliminate risk, it only spreads the financial burden.
questions.p: Insurance na arrangement wey many people dey contribute small money (premium) go one fund, and anybody wey loss happen to go collect compensation from the fund. E no dey remove risk, e just dey share the money wahala.

questions.q: Which principle of insurance requires that both the insurer and the insured must disclose all material facts that could affect the decision to grant or accept the policy, even without being specifically asked?
o: Utmost good faith
Indemnity
Contribution
Subrogation
questions.e: Utmost good faith (uberrimae fidei) demands full and honest disclosure of all relevant facts by both parties before a policy is agreed. Hiding important information can make the contract void.
questions.p: Utmost good faith mean say both insurance company and the person wey dey insure must tell each other all important facts, even if nobody ask am. If you hide important info, the policy fit no valid.

questions.q: The principle which states that an insured person should be restored to the same financial position he was in before the loss occurred, and should not profit from a claim, is known as the principle of:
o: Insurable interest
Proximate cause
Indemnity
Contribution
questions.e: Indemnity means the insurer compensates the insured only to the extent of the actual loss suffered, so the insured neither gains nor loses financially from the claim.
questions.p: Indemnity mean say the insurance company go pay you back only for the exact loss wey you suffer, no more no less, so you no go make extra profit from the claim.

questions.q: After paying Mrs Adaeze compensation for her car damaged by a careless driver, her insurance company takes over her legal right to sue the driver for the damages. This action illustrates the principle of:
o: Utmost good faith
Average
Insurable interest
Subrogation
questions.e: Subrogation allows an insurer who has paid a claim to step into the insured's position and recover the loss from the party responsible, so the insured does not collect twice for the same loss.
questions.p: Subrogation na when insurance company wey don pay claim take over the person right to chase the one wey cause the damage, so that the insured no go collect money two times for the same loss.

questions.q: Which of the following is correctly classified as a type of life assurance policy?
o: Fire insurance
Endowment assurance
Marine insurance
Fidelity guarantee insurance
questions.e: Endowment assurance is a life assurance policy that pays a lump sum either on the death of the policyholder or at the end of an agreed term, whichever comes first. Fire, marine and fidelity policies are types of general (non-life) insurance.
questions.p: Endowment assurance na life assurance wey dey pay lump sum money either when the person die or when the agreed period finish, whichever come first. Fire, marine and fidelity na general insurance, no be life assurance.

questions.q: For a contract of insurance to be legally valid, the policyholder must have a financial relationship with the subject matter of insurance such that he would suffer a genuine loss if the insured event occurs. This requirement is called:
o: Insurable interest
Indemnity
Proximate cause
Contribution
questions.e: Insurable interest means the insured must stand to lose financially if the insured event happens; without it, an insurance contract is treated as a form of gambling and is not valid.
questions.p: Insurable interest mean say the person wey dey insure must get financial connection to the thing wey e dey insure, so if the bad event happen, e go really suffer loss. Without this one, the insurance go just be like gambling and e no go valid.

questions.q: Zenith Insurance and Leadway Assurance both cover the same warehouse against fire risk at the same time. Zenith's policy covers ₦200,000 while Leadway's policy covers ₦300,000 on the same property. A fire outbreak causes a loss of ₦100,000. Under the principle of contribution, how much will Zenith Insurance pay?
questions.e: Contribution shares a loss between insurers in proportion to their cover. Total sum insured = 200,000 + 300,000 = 500,000. Zenith's share = (200,000/500,000) x 100,000 = ₦40,000, preventing the insured from being paid twice for one loss.
questions.p: Contribution dey share loss among the insurance companies based on how much each one cover. Total cover = 200,000 + 300,000 = 500,000. Zenith own share = (200,000/500,000) x 100,000 = ₦40,000, so the person no go collect double pay for one loss.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a recognised mode of transportation for moving goods from one place to another?
o: Telegraph transmission
Road transport
Rail transport
Water transport
questions.e: Transportation moves physical goods using means like road, rail, water, air or pipeline. Telegraph is a means of sending messages, not goods, so it is not a mode of transportation.
questions.p: Transportation na about how dem dey carry goods comot one place go another place, like road, rail or water. Telegraph na for sending message, e no fit carry goods, so e no be transport mode.

questions.q: What is the main function of warehousing in commerce?
o: To permanently transfer ownership of goods to buyers
To store goods safely until they are required
To advertise goods to final consumers
To produce goods in large quantities
questions.e: Warehousing deals with keeping goods in a safe place after production until they are needed by consumers or traders. It bridges the gap in time between production and consumption.
questions.p: Warehouse na where dem dey keep goods well-well after dem don produce am, until the time wey people go need am. E dey help cover the gap between production time and when people go buy am.

questions.q: Which document is issued by a shipping company as evidence of a contract of carriage and acknowledges receipt of goods for transport by sea?
o: Invoice
Certificate of origin
Waybill
Bill of lading
questions.e: The bill of lading is a special document used in sea transport. It serves as a receipt for goods shipped, evidence of the contract of carriage, and a document of title to the goods.
questions.p: Bill of lading na the correct paper wey shipping company dey give. E dey show say dem don collect the goods, e be like contract paper, and e fit transfer ownership of the goods too.

questions.q: One major advantage of pipeline transport over road transport when moving crude oil or gas over very long distances is that pipeline transport:
o: Is generally cheaper per unit for bulk liquids or gases over long distances
Can carry passengers together with the goods
Is flexible enough to reach every remote village
Requires frequent loading and unloading at stations
questions.e: Pipelines are built specifically for continuous movement of liquids and gases in bulk, so once installed, the cost per unit over long distances becomes very low compared to road transport which needs many trucks, drivers and fuel.
questions.p: Pipeline dey good well-well to carry liquid or gas for long distance because once dem build am, e go cheap pass road wey need plenty truck, driver and fuel to move the same quantity.

questions.q: Which type of warehouse is specifically used to store imported goods on which import duty has not yet been paid by the importer?
o: Cold storage warehouse
Bonded warehouse
Private warehouse
Public warehouse
questions.e: A bonded warehouse is a government-licensed facility where imported goods can be stored before import duties are paid, allowing importers to delay payment until the goods are actually released for sale.
questions.p: Bonded warehouse na the special store wey government approve, where dem dey keep imported goods before the importer pay duty. The duty no dey pay until the goods comot from there.

questions.q: Mama Ngozi wants to move fresh tomatoes from Kano to Lagos as quickly as possible so they do not spoil before reaching the market. Which mode of transport would best serve her purpose, despite its higher cost?
o: Water transport
Pipeline transport
Air transport
Rail transport
questions.e: Perishable goods like tomatoes spoil quickly, so speed matters more than cost. Air transport is the fastest mode over long distances, reducing the time the tomatoes spend in transit and protecting their quality, even though it costs more than other options.
questions.p: Since tomatoes dey quick spoil, wetin dey important be say the journey go fast reach, no be say e go cheap. Air transport na the fastest way to carry am quick reach Lagos make e no spoil, even though e cost more.

questions.q: Which of the following is a genuine disadvantage of road transport in Nigeria?
o: Lower cost of operation over short distances
Flexibility in scheduling trips at any convenient time
Ability to reach remote villages easily
High cost of maintenance due to accidents and poor road conditions
questions.e: Road transport often suffers from bad roads, frequent accidents, and vehicle breakdowns, which increase maintenance costs for vehicle owners. The other options listed are actually advantages of road transport, not disadvantages.
questions.p: Road transport get problem of bad road and accident wey dey make vehicle maintenance cost high. The other options na advantage of road transport, no be wahala.

questions.q: Warehousing is often described as a value-adding service in commerce mainly because it:
o: Creates time utility by making goods available whenever they are needed
Permanently transfers ownership of goods from seller to buyer
Reduces the actual quantity of goods that were produced
Increases the physical size of the goods stored
questions.e: Value in commerce can be added through form, place, time or possession utility. Warehousing adds time utility because it holds goods safely between production and the moment they are actually demanded, making them available exactly when consumers need them.
questions.p: Commerce fit add value through form, place, time or possession. Warehouse dey add time value because e dey keep goods well until the time wey consumer go need am, so e go dey available anytime wey dem want am.

questions.q: Which of the following best defines communication in business studies?
o: act of storing documents safely in a warehouse
process of transmitting and exchanging information between a sender and receiver using a common medium
process of selling goods on credit to trusted customers
process of moving goods from producer to final consumer
questions.e: Communication is the exchange of information, ideas or feelings between a sender and a receiver using a medium that both understand. The other options describe distribution, storage and credit sale, not communication.
questions.p: Communication na when sender dey pass message give receiver through medium wey both of dem understand. The other options dey talk about moving goods, storing papers, and credit sale, no be communication.

questions.q: In the communication process, which of these is NOT one of the basic elements needed for communication to take place?
o: Receiver
Sender
Feedback
Warehouse
questions.e: The basic elements of communication are sender, message, medium, receiver and feedback. A warehouse is a storage facility used in trade, not a communication element.
questions.p: The key parts of communication na sender, message, medium, receiver and feedback. Warehouse na storage place for goods, e no be part of communication.

questions.q: Mrs. Adaeze in Enugu wants to send a small sum of money to her son in Abuja through the post office, but she does not operate a bank account. Which postal service is most suitable for her?
o: Telex
Franking machine
Postal order
Courier waybill
questions.e: A postal order is a document bought at the post office that allows one to send money safely through the post without needing a bank account. Telex and franking machines are not for sending money, and a courier waybill is used to track parcels, not transfer cash.
questions.p: Postal order na paper wey you fit buy for post office to send money safely without bank account. Telex and franking machine no be for sending money, and courier waybill na for tracking parcel, no be cash transfer.

questions.q: NIPOST, the government agency responsible for postal services in Nigeria, stands for what?
o: National Institute of Postal Services and Telecommunications
Nigerian Postal Service
Nigerian Postal and Stamp Trust
Nigeria Information and Postal Service Trust
questions.e: NIPOST stands for Nigerian Postal Service, the government body that handles mail collection, sorting and delivery across Nigeria. The other options are made-up names that do not match the real agency.
questions.p: NIPOST na Nigerian Postal Service, the government body wey dey handle mail collection, sorting and delivery for Nigeria. The other options na names wey no match the real agency.

questions.q: What is the main advantage of sending an important letter by registered mail instead of ordinary mail?
o: it does not require an address label
it is cheaper than ordinary mail
it travels faster than ordinary mail
sender gets proof of posting and compensation if the letter is lost
questions.e: Registered mail is recorded at the post office, so the sender has proof it was posted and can be compensated if it gets lost or damaged. It is usually not faster or cheaper than ordinary mail, and it still needs a proper address label.
questions.p: Registered mail dem dey record for post office, so sender get proof say e post am and fit collect compensation if the letter miss or spoil. E no dey always faster or cheaper pass ordinary mail, and e still need correct address label.

questions.q: Chief Okoro in Lagos needs to send an important original certificate to a client in Kano and wants same-day, door-to-door delivery with the ability to track the parcel. Which service best meets his need?
o: Courier service
Ordinary letter mail
Telegram
Postal order
questions.e: Courier services offer fast, door-to-door delivery with tracking, making them ideal for urgent and valuable items like original certificates. Ordinary mail is slower and has no tracking, a postal order is for sending money, and a telegram only carries short text messages.
questions.p: Courier service dey give fast, door-to-door delivery with tracking, so e better for urgent and important papers like original certificate. Ordinary mail dey slow with no tracking, postal order na for sending money, and telegram na for short text message only.

questions.q: In the communication process, the term 'noise' refers to what?
o: the feedback given by the receiver
loud background sound only
any factor that distorts or interferes with the message between sender and receiver
the physical channel used to send the message
questions.e: In communication studies, noise means any disturbance, such as poor network, wrong language, or distractions, that prevents the message from being received clearly, not just loud sound. The other options describe different parts of the communication process, not noise.
questions.p: For communication, noise mean anything wey fit spoil or confuse the message between sender and receiver, like bad network, wrong language, or distraction, no be only loud sound. The other options dey describe other parts of communication process, no be noise.

questions.q: A traveling trader who has no fixed home address wants to collect his letters directly at a post office counter whenever he visits a particular town. This postal facility is called?
o: Poste restante
Recorded delivery
Franking
Cash on delivery
questions.e: Poste restante is a postal service that allows letters to be kept at a specific post office for collection by a person without a fixed address. Recorded delivery, cash on delivery, and franking are different postal features that do not serve this exact purpose.
questions.p: Poste restante na postal service wey allow letters stay for particular post office make person wey no get fixed address fit come collect am. Recorded delivery, cash on delivery, and franking na different postal features wey no dey serve this kain purpose.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes a sole proprietorship business?
o: A business owned and run by the government for public service
A business formed by two or more persons who sign a deed of partnership
A business owned and managed by a single individual who provides capital, bears all risks and takes all profits
A business owned by many shareholders who buy shares in it
questions.e: A sole proprietorship is a one-man business. The owner supplies the capital, makes all decisions, takes all the profit and also bears all the losses and risks alone.
questions.p: Sole proprietorship na business wey one person dey own. E be the one wey bring money, e dey control everything, e dey chop the profit and e dey carry the loss too.

questions.q: In a sole proprietorship, the owner is often called the sole trader because
o: He must register the business with the Corporate Affairs Commission before he can start trading
He alone provides the capital, bears the risk and controls the entire business
He is appointed by government officials to manage the business on their behalf
He shares the profit of the business equally with his employees
questions.e: The word 'sole' means 'only one'. The sole trader is the only owner, so he alone contributes capital, controls the business and bears the risk of success or failure.
questions.p: 'Sole' mean 'only one person'. So na the sole trader alone dey bring capital, dey control the business and e be im one dey carry the risk.

questions.q: Which of these is a major advantage that a sole proprietorship has over a partnership business?
o: Business losses are shared among many owners, reducing individual burden
It enjoys perpetual existence even after the owner dies
It can raise larger amounts of capital for expansion
Decisions can be made quickly since only one person controls the business
questions.e: Because a sole proprietor does not need to consult partners, he can take decisions fast, which is an advantage over partnerships where decisions may be delayed due to consultation among partners.
questions.p: Since na one person dey run the business, im fit take decision sharp sharp without to dey consult other people, unlike partnership wey all partners go first discuss before decision.

questions.q: Mama Chidinma runs a provision store alone as a sole trader. If the business fails and its debts are more than the value of the business assets, what will happen to her personal properties such as her car and house?
o: They are fully protected by law from the business creditors
The government will seize them and hold them in trust for her
They can be sold by creditors to offset the outstanding business debts
They will automatically be shared among her relatives to settle the debt
questions.e: A sole proprietor has unlimited liability. This means there is no legal separation between her personal and business assets, so creditors can go after her personal property to recover unpaid business debts.
questions.p: Sole trader get unlimited liability. E mean say im business property and im personal property na the same thing for law, so creditors fit sell im personal things like car and house make dem recover their money.

questions.q: The written document that spells out the terms and conditions guiding the operation of a partnership, such as how profits will be shared and how capital will be contributed, is called the
o: Partnership deed
Memorandum of association
Certificate of incorporation
Prospectus
questions.e: The partnership deed (also called articles of partnership) is the agreement signed by partners stating how the business will operate, including profit-sharing ratios and capital contributions.
questions.p: Partnership deed na the paper wey the partners sign wey dey show how dem go share profit, how dem go bring capital and how the business go run.

questions.q: Alhaji Musa and Mr. Eze formed a partnership business. Their partnership deed states that profit should be shared in the ratio 3:2 between Alhaji Musa and Mr. Eze respectively. If the business made a total profit of ₦150,000 for the year, how much will Alhaji Musa receive?
questions.e: The ratio 3:2 has a total of 5 parts. Alhaji Musa's share is 3 parts out of 5, so his amount is (3/5) x 150,000 = 90,000.
questions.p: 3:2 ratio get total of 5 parts. Alhaji Musa own na 3 parts out of 5, so im money na (3/5) x 150,000 wey be 90,000.

questions.q: Under Nigerian company law (Companies and Allied Matters Act), what is the maximum number of persons generally allowed to form an ordinary trading partnership, excluding special professional partnerships such as law or accounting firms?
o: 10 persons
50 persons
There is no maximum limit
20 persons
questions.e: Nigerian law generally limits ordinary trading partnerships to a maximum of 20 persons, though certain professional partnerships like law firms and accounting firms may exceed this limit.
questions.p: Nigerian law talk say ordinary trading partnership no suppose pass 20 persons, but some professional ones like lawyers and accountants fit pass that number.

questions.q: A joint stock company is best described as a form of business organisation that is owned by:
o: Shareholders who have bought shares in the company
A single individual who bears all risk
Workers who contribute labour only
The government on behalf of citizens
questions.e: A joint stock company raises capital by selling shares to the public, and those who buy the shares (shareholders) become the owners. This is different from sole proprietorship or government-owned enterprises.
questions.p: Joint stock company na business wey dem dey own through shares wey people buy. The people wey buy the shares na dem be shareholders, so dem be the owners.

questions.q: Which of the following is a major advantage of a public limited liability company over a private limited liability company?
o: It can be formed by only one person
It can sell its shares directly to members of the public on the stock exchange
It is not required to publish its accounts
It is exempted from paying company tax
questions.e: A public limited company can invite the general public to buy its shares, often through the stock exchange, allowing it to raise large amounts of capital. A private company cannot do this.
questions.p: Public limited company fit sell im shares to general public, sometimes through stock exchange, so e fit raise big money. Private company no fit do dis one.

questions.q: Which of the following is a key principle of cooperative societies that distinguishes them from joint stock companies?
o: Members cannot withdraw their savings once contributed
Profit is shared strictly according to the number of shares held by each member
Voting in general meetings is based on 'one member, one vote' regardless of capital contributed
Only the government can be a member of a cooperative society
questions.e: In cooperative societies, democratic control is practised, so every member has equal voting power (one member, one vote), unlike joint stock companies where voting power often depends on the number of shares owned.
questions.p: For cooperative society, na one man one vote dem dey use, no matter how much money the person contribute. Dis one different from joint stock company wey voting dey depend on shares wey person get.

questions.q: A statutory corporation such as the Nigerian Ports Authority is set up mainly to:
o: Maximise profit for private shareholders
Avoid any form of government supervision
Compete freely with private companies without any regulation
Provide essential services and goods for public welfare under government control
questions.e: Statutory corporations (public enterprises) are established by an Act of Parliament or Decree to provide essential services to the public, often in areas like ports, power and transport, under government control, rather than purely to make profit for private owners.
questions.p: Statutory corporation like Nigerian Ports Authority, gofment dey establish am to provide important service for public under gofment control, e no be say na only profit dem dey chase.

questions.q: Which of these is a major disadvantage of a joint stock company when compared with a sole proprietorship?
o: It automatically ceases to exist when one shareholder dies
It has unlimited access to large capital from many shareholders
It usually requires more complex legal procedures and documentation to set up
It allows for easy and quick decision-making by one owner
questions.e: Setting up a joint stock company involves legal requirements such as registration with the Corporate Affairs Commission, preparation of memorandum and articles of association, which make it more complex and costly to start than a sole proprietorship.
questions.p: To start joint stock company, you go need register am well well with CAC and prepare many legal papers, e no be like sole proprietorship wey one person fit just start am quick quick.

questions.q: Adaeze Multipurpose Cooperative Society in Enugu made a surplus of ₦600,000 at the end of the year. The society's rule states that 1/3 of the surplus goes to a reserve fund, and the remaining amount is shared equally among its 20 members as dividend. How much will each member receive?
questions.e: Reserve fund = 1/3 of 600,000 = 200,000, leaving 600,000 - 200,000 = 400,000 to be shared. Dividing 400,000 among 20 members gives 400,000 / 20 = ₦20,000 per member.
questions.p: Reserve fund na 1/3 of 600,000 wey be 200,000, so wetin remain na 400,000. If you divide 400,000 give 20 members, each one go get 20,000 naira.

questions.q: A key reason why some public enterprises in Nigeria have been privatised or commercialised is that:
o: Private owners are legally forbidden from owning large businesses
Many of them were inefficient and relied heavily on government subsidy
They were making too much profit for the government to manage
Government wanted to reduce the number of private limited companies
questions.e: Many public enterprises became loss-making and depended on government subsidies due to poor management and lack of competition, so government introduced privatisation and commercialisation to improve efficiency and reduce the burden on public funds.
questions.p: Plenty public enterprises for Nigeria no dey efficient and dem dey depend on gofment subsidy because of bad management, so gofment decide to privatise or commercialise dem make dem perform better.

questions.q: Which of the following is mainly a source of long-term capital for a business?
o: Trade credit
Bank overdraft
Commercial paper
Debenture
questions.e: A debenture is a long-term loan certificate that a company repays over many years, so it is a long-term source of capital. Trade credit, bank overdraft and commercial paper are all short-term sources of finance.
questions.p: Debenture na long-term loan paper wey company dey pay back over plenty years, so e be long-term capital. Trade credit, overdraft and commercial paper na short-term finance.

questions.q: Money set aside by a business to acquire fixed assets such as land, buildings and machinery that will be used repeatedly over many years is called ____.
o: Working capital
Loan capital
Fixed capital
Circulating capital
questions.e: Fixed capital is the money invested in assets that stay in the business for a long time, like land and machinery. Working capital is for day-to-day running of the business, not for buying long-lasting assets.
questions.p: Fixed capital na money wey dem use buy things wey go stay long time for business, like land and machine. Working capital na for daily running of business, e no be for buying long-lasting asset.

questions.q: Mrs Adeyemi's provision shop in Ibadan recorded sales of ₦450,000 in January, ₦380,000 in February and ₦520,000 in March. Calculate her total turnover for the three months.
questions.e: Turnover is the total value of sales over a period. Add the three months together: 450,000 + 380,000 + 520,000 = 1,350,000.
questions.p: Turnover na total sales for the period. Add the three months: 450,000 + 380,000 + 520,000 = 1,350,000.

questions.q: A trader in Onitsha bought a consignment of goods for ₦85,000 and sold the whole consignment for ₦110,000. Calculate the profit made on the transaction.
questions.e: Profit is the difference between selling price and cost price. 110,000 - 85,000 = 25,000.
questions.p: Profit na the difference between the price wey you sell am and the price wey you buy am. 110,000 minus 85,000 = 25,000.

questions.q: Chinedu's electronics business had total sales of ₦600,000 for the month, while the cost of the goods sold was ₦420,000. Calculate the gross profit for the month.
questions.e: Gross profit = Sales - Cost of goods sold. So 600,000 - 420,000 = 180,000.
questions.p: Gross profit na Sales minus Cost of goods wey you sell. So 600,000 minus 420,000 = 180,000.

questions.q: A trading company recorded sales of ₦2,000,000, cost of goods sold of ₦1,200,000, and operating expenses (such as rent, salaries and transport) of ₦350,000 for the year. Calculate the company's net profit for the year.
questions.e: First find gross profit: 2,000,000 - 1,200,000 = 800,000. Net profit = Gross profit - operating expenses = 800,000 - 350,000 = 450,000.
questions.p: First find gross profit: 2,000,000 minus 1,200,000 = 800,000. Net profit na gross profit minus expenses: 800,000 minus 350,000 = 450,000.

questions.q: A business has total assets of ₦3,000,000 and total liabilities (excluding the owner's capital) of ₦1,200,000. If the business made a net profit of ₦360,000 for the year, calculate the return on capital employed (as a percentage), where capital employed = total assets minus total liabilities.
questions.p: Capital employed = 3,000,000 minus 1,200,000 = 1,800,000. Return on capital employed = (360,000 divide by 1,800,000) x 100 = 20%.

questions.q: A supermarket has current assets (cash, stock and debtors) of ₦750,000 and current liabilities (creditors and short-term loans) of ₦450,000. Calculate the supermarket's working capital.
questions.e: Working capital = Current assets - Current liabilities = 750,000 - 450,000 = 300,000. This shows the money available for day-to-day running of the business.
questions.p: Working capital = Current assets minus Current liabilities = 750,000 minus 450,000 = 300,000. Na the money wey dey available for daily running of the business.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes a stock exchange?
o: An organised market where existing shares, bonds and other securities are bought and sold
A warehouse where manufactured goods are stored before sale
A market where new companies register their business names
A government agency that prints new currency notes
questions.e: A stock exchange is a well organised market where securities that have already been issued, such as shares and bonds, are bought and sold by investors. It does not register companies or store goods.
questions.p: Stock exchange na market wey dem dey buy and sell shares, bonds and other securities wey don already dey market. E no be place wey dem dey register company or store goods.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT a security that can be traded on the Nigerian stock exchange?
o: Debentures
Ordinary shares
Government bonds
A sales invoice
questions.e: Shares, bonds and debentures are financial instruments traded on the stock exchange to raise capital. A sales invoice is just a business document showing goods sold, not a security.
questions.p: Shares, bonds and debentures na securities wey dem dey trade for stock exchange to raise money. Sales invoice na just paper wey show say dem don sell goods, e no be security.

questions.q: Chidinma buys shares in Dangote Cement because she believes the price will rise soon, so she can sell later at a profit. In stock exchange language, Chidinma is acting as a...
o: Bear
Bull
Stag
Jobber
questions.e: A bull is an investor who buys shares expecting prices to rise so as to sell later at a higher price. A bear expects prices to fall, while a stag applies for new shares hoping to sell them quickly at a profit.
questions.p: Bull na person wey buy shares because e dey expect say price go rise so e fit sell am later make profit. Bear na person wey dey expect price to fall, stag na person wey dey apply for new shares to quick sell am make quick profit.

questions.q: When a public limited company offers new shares for the first time to raise fresh capital, these shares are sold in the...
o: Foreign exchange market
Secondary market
Primary market
Money market
questions.e: The primary market is where new securities are issued for the first time directly by the company to raise fresh capital. Once issued, these securities are later traded among investors in the secondary market.
questions.p: Primary market na where new securities dey first enter market, as company dey sell am direct to raise new money. After that, people go dey buy and sell am among themselves for secondary market.

questions.q: A company declares a dividend of ₦2.50 per share. If the current market price of the share is ₦25.00, what is the dividend yield?
questions.e: Dividend yield = (dividend per share / market price per share) x 100 = (2.50/25.00) x 100 = 10%. This tells an investor the percentage return earned from dividends relative to the share's market price.
questions.p: Dividend yield = (dividend wey dem pay / market price) x 100 = (2.50/25.00) x 100 = 10%. Na im show the percentage wey investor dey earn from dividend compare to the price wey e buy the share.

questions.q: Which functionary on the stock exchange buys and sells securities on behalf of clients and earns a commission for this service?
o: Underwriter
Jobber
Stockbroker
Registrar
questions.e: A stockbroker acts as an agent between the investing public and the stock exchange, buying and selling securities for clients and charging a commission. A jobber, by contrast, trades securities on his own account for profit.
questions.p: Stockbroker na person wey dey represent client, e dey buy and sell securities for the client and e dey collect commission. Jobber na different person wey dey buy and sell securities for himself make profit.

questions.q: Adaku Plc has 100,000 ordinary shares of ₦1 each in issue. The company decides to raise more capital through a rights issue of 1 new share for every 4 shares already held, at a price of ₦1.20 per new share. How much money will the rights issue raise in total?
questions.e: Number of new shares = 100,000 / 4 = 25,000 shares. Amount raised = 25,000 x ₦1.20 = ₦30,000. A rights issue allows existing shareholders to buy extra shares at a fixed ratio and price before outsiders.
