questions.p: New shares wey go come = 100,000 divide by 4 = 25,000 shares. Money wey go raise = 25,000 x ₦1.20 = ₦30,000. Rights issue na when old shareholders get first chance to buy extra shares for fixed price before any outsider.

questions.q: Which statement correctly distinguishes a debenture holder from an ordinary shareholder of a company?
o: A debenture holder is a part-owner of the company while a shareholder is a creditor
A debenture holder is a creditor of the company while a shareholder is a part-owner
Both debenture holders and ordinary shareholders always receive a fixed annual dividend
Debenture holders have voting rights at the company's annual general meeting while shareholders do not
questions.e: A debenture holder lends money to the company and is therefore a creditor entitled to fixed interest, whether or not the company makes profit. An ordinary shareholder is a part-owner of the company and receives dividends only when profits are made and declared.
questions.p: Debenture holder na person wey lend company money, so e be creditor wey suppose collect fixed interest whether company get profit or not. Ordinary shareholder na part-owner of the company and e go only collect dividend if company get profit wey dem declare.

questions.q: A trade association is best described as a body formed by firms engaged in the same line of business mainly to:
o: Protect and promote the common interests of its members
Organise consumers to boycott certain goods
Act as a government agency that fixes prices for goods
Serve as a labour union for factory workers
questions.e: A trade association is a voluntary body of firms or traders in the same industry who join together to protect and promote their common business interests, such as sharing information and negotiating with government.
questions.p: Trade association na group wey business people wey dey do the same kain work come form together, so dem go fit protect and push their common interest, like how dem go dey yarn with government.

questions.q: The acronym NACCIMA, a well-known umbrella body for business organisations in Nigeria, stands for:
o: Nigerian Agency for Consumer and Commercial Industry Matters
Nigerian Association of Chambers of Commerce, Industry, Mines and Agriculture
National Council of Commerce and Industry in Mining Affairs
National Association for Chambers of Commerce, Insurance and Marketing Affairs
questions.e: NACCIMA stands for Nigerian Association of Chambers of Commerce, Industry, Mines and Agriculture, which is a national umbrella organisation that brings together various chambers of commerce and trade bodies across Nigeria.
questions.p: NACCIMA mean Nigerian Association of Chambers of Commerce, Industry, Mines and Agriculture. Na the big umbrella body wey dey join different chambers of commerce and trade bodies for Nigeria together.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a typical function performed by a chamber of commerce for its members?
o: Organising trade fairs and exhibitions
Representing business interests to government
Manufacturing goods for sale to the public
Settling trade disputes among members
questions.e: A chamber of commerce is an association that promotes trade, settles disputes, organises fairs and speaks to government on behalf of businesses; it does not itself manufacture or sell goods, since that is the role of individual member firms.
questions.p: Chamber of commerce na body wey dey push trade, settle wahala, organise trade fair and talk for business people front of government; e no be manufacturer, na the member companies dey make and sell their own goods.

questions.q: A major function of the Consumer Protection Council (or similar consumer protection agency) in Nigeria is to:
o: Investigate complaints from consumers against poor quality or harmful goods
Grant soft loans to small-scale traders
Fix minimum wage for workers in private companies
Issue import licences to foreign companies
questions.e: Consumer protection agencies exist mainly to safeguard the interest of buyers by receiving and investigating complaints about substandard, unsafe or harmful goods and services sold to the public.
questions.p: Consumer protection agency work na to protect the buyer, so dem dey receive and investigate complain wey consumers bring about bad quality or harmful goods wey dem buy.

questions.q: One major advantage a small trader, Mama Ngozi, enjoys by joining her local traders' association is that the association can:
o: Provide free transportation of her goods across states
Automatically exempt her from paying company income tax
Guarantee her a direct government supply contract
Give members collective bargaining power to get better terms from suppliers
questions.e: Trade associations negotiate on behalf of many small traders at once, so members often get better prices, credit terms or discounts from suppliers than they could get bargaining alone.
questions.p: Trade association dey yarn with suppliers for behalf of plenty traders together, so members fit get better price, credit or discount pass if na them one go bargain alone.

questions.q: Some soap manufacturers in Aba form a trade association and then secretly agree among themselves to fix a high common price and limit the quantity of soap each member produces. This action would most likely lead to:
o: Exploitation of consumers through higher prices and reduced choice
A reduction in soap prices due to healthy competition
Automatic increase in the quality of soap produced
Improved bargaining power for consumers over the manufacturers
questions.e: When members of a trade association collude to fix prices and restrict output, they behave like a cartel, which harms consumers by raising prices and limiting the amount and variety of goods available; this is exactly the kind of practice consumer protection bodies try to prevent.
questions.p: If the soap makers come join hand fix high price and limit how much soap dem go produce, na cartel behaviour be that, and e go make price go up and consumer go get less choice, that na why consumer protection body dey fight this kain gragra.

questions.q: The key difference between a trade association and a trade union is that:
o: Trade association fixes workers' wages while trade union fixes consumer prices
Trade association represents consumers while trade union represents employers
Trade association is for employers or firms in the same trade while trade union is for workers or employees
Trade association and trade union are formed only by the government
questions.e: A trade association is made up of business owners or firms in the same line of trade protecting business interests, while a trade union is made up of employees who join together to protect workers' welfare and bargain with employers over wages and conditions.
questions.p: Trade association na for business owners or company wey dey do same trade, dem dey protect business interest; trade union na for workers wey join hand protect their welfare and bargain with employer for wages and condition of service.

questions.q: Which of the following is recognised as a basic right of consumers that consumer protection laws seek to guarantee?
o: The right to personally fix the selling price of goods bought in a shop
The right to safety from goods that are hazardous to health
The right to stop other consumers from buying certain goods
The right to manufacture competing products freely without registration
questions.e: One of the basic rights of a consumer is the right to safety, meaning they should be protected from goods and services that could harm their health or life, such as expired drugs or unsafe electrical appliances.
questions.p: One of the basic right wey consumer get na right to safety, meaning say make dem no suffer from goods wey fit harm their body, like expired medicine or bad electrical gadget.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the basic functions of management as identified by classical management theorists such as Henri Fayol?
o: Planning
Controlling
Organising
Marketing
questions.e: Fayol's classical functions of management are planning, organising, commanding/directing, coordinating and controlling. Marketing is a specific business function (like production or finance), not a general management function.
questions.p: Fayol im management functions na planning, organising, directing, coordinating and controlling. Marketing na business function wey dey under one department, e no be general management function.

questions.q: In a typical business organisation, the level of management that is directly responsible for the day-to-day supervision of workers on the factory floor is called the:
o: Board of directors
Top management
Lower (supervisory) management
Middle management
questions.e: Lower or supervisory management works closest to the workers and handles daily, routine supervision of operations. Top management sets overall policy, while middle management coordinates between the two levels.
questions.p: Lower or supervisory management na dem dey close to di workers, dem dey handle daily, normal supervision of work. Top management na dem dey set big policy, middle management dey connect top and lower level.

questions.q: Mrs Adaeze, the Managing Director of a Lagos-based bakery, has the Production Manager, Sales Manager and Finance Manager reporting directly to her. The number of people who report directly to Mrs Adaeze is referred to as her:
o: Line of authority
Span of control
Delegation ratio
Scalar chain
questions.e: Span of control is the number of subordinates that a manager directly supervises. Here, Mrs Adaeze directly supervises three managers, so her span of control is 3.
questions.p: Span of control na di number of people wey dey report directly to one manager. Mrs Adaeze get three managers wey dey report to am, so her span of control na three.

questions.q: A company structures its staff into separate departments such as Production, Marketing, Finance and Human Resources, with each department head being an expert in that specific area. This type of organisational structure is called:
o: Line organisation
Committee organisation
Matrix organisation
Functional organisation
questions.e: Functional organisation groups workers according to the specialised activity or function they perform, such as marketing or finance. This allows specialists to head each department based on their expertise.
questions.p: Functional organisation na when dem group workers based on di specific work wey dem dey do, like marketing or finance. Na why specialist dey head each department.

questions.q: The management principle which states that each employee should receive orders from only one superior at a time is known as the principle of:
o: Unity of command
Scalar chain
Span of control
Division of labour
questions.e: Unity of command means every worker should take instructions from one boss only, to avoid confusion and conflicting orders. This principle was strongly emphasised by Henri Fayol.
questions.p: Unity of command mean say each worker suppose dey take order from just one boss, so dat confusion no go dey. Na Fayol talk am well well.

questions.q: A trading company reorganised its staff so that the Marketing Manager gives marketing instructions to workers in every department, while the Production Manager gives production instructions to the same workers. Soon, many workers began receiving conflicting orders from both managers on the same day. This confusion is a common weakness of which type of organisational structure?
o: Line organisation
Functional organisation
Decentralised organisation
Line and staff organisation
questions.e: In functional organisation, specialist managers give orders across departments based on their area of expertise, which can break the principle of unity of command and cause conflicting instructions to the same workers. This is a well-known drawback of pure functional structures compared to line organisation.
questions.p: For functional organisation, different specialist managers dey give order for different departments based on their area, so dem fit break unity of command and workers go dey confuse with different order. Na common wahala for functional structure pass line organisation.

questions.q: Delegation of authority in an organisation best means that a manager:
o: Gives up all control and responsibility over a department forever
Employs new staff to replace an underperforming worker
Permanently transfers ownership of the business to a subordinate
Gives a subordinate the right to take certain decisions within set limits, while the manager remains ultimately responsible
questions.e: Delegation means a manager passes down specific authority to a subordinate to make decisions within agreed limits, but the manager still carries final responsibility for the outcome. It does not mean giving away ownership or permanent control.
questions.p: Delegation mean say manager go give subordinate small power make e fit take some decision within di limit wey dem agree, but di manager still carry final responsibility. E no mean say manager don give away ownership forever.

questions.q: Alhaji Musa's transport company has 1 General Manager who directly supervises 3 Branch Managers. Each of the 3 Branch Managers directly supervises 6 drivers. What is the total number of people in the company, including the General Manager?
questions.e: Total = General Manager + Branch Managers + Drivers = 1 + 3 + (3 x 6) = 1 + 3 + 18 = 22. Counting every level of the organisation gives 22 people in total.
questions.p: Total = General Manager + Branch Managers + Drivers = 1 + 3 + (3 x 6) = 1 + 3 + 18 = 22. If you count everybody for di organisation structure, you go reach 22 people.

questions.q: What is the main focus of the modern marketing concept as practised by businesses in Nigeria?
o: Selling whatever the factory produces
Producing goods as cheaply as possible
Satisfying customer needs and wants profitably
Increasing the number of advertisements only
questions.e: The marketing concept puts the customer first, aiming to identify and satisfy their needs while still making profit for the business. It is different from just focusing on production or pushing sales.
questions.p: Marketing concept mean say business go first find out wetin customer want, then satisfy am make profit still enter. E no be just to produce cheap or push sell-sell.

questions.q: The marketing mix is often summarised as the '4Ps'. Which of the following is NOT one of the 4Ps?
o: Price
Product
Profit
Place
questions.e: The 4Ps of marketing are Product, Price, Place and Promotion. Profit is a business goal but it is not one of the 4Ps elements of the marketing mix.
questions.p: The 4Ps na Product, Price, Place and Promotion. Profit na result wey business dey find, but e no be part of the 4Ps.

questions.q: Which element of the marketing mix is concerned with the channels used to move goods from the producer to the final consumer?
o: Promotion
Product
Price
Place
questions.e: Place deals with distribution, that is, how goods move from the producer, through middlemen like wholesalers and retailers, to reach the final consumer. Product is about the item itself, while Price and Promotion are different elements.
questions.p: Place na the one wey dey handle how goods dey waka comot from producer reach the final consumer, through wholesalers and retailers. Product na about the item, Price na cost, Promotion na how dem advertise am.

questions.q: A furniture maker in Aba reduces the cost of his chairs during the Christmas season so that more customers can afford to buy. This decision mainly concerns which element of the marketing mix?
o: Place
Price
Promotion
Product
questions.e: Reducing the amount customers pay for the chairs is a pricing decision, since price refers to the amount charged for a product. It is not about changing the product itself, its distribution, or its advertisement.
questions.p: To reduce how much customer go pay na Price decision, because Price na the amount wey dem dey charge for product. E no be about the chair design, how e dey reach market, or advert.

questions.q: Which of the following activities by a soft drink company best illustrates the 'promotion' element of the marketing mix?
o: Running a radio jingle to inform customers about the drink
Designing a new bottle shape for the drink
Building a warehouse closer to retailers in Kano
Charging ₦150 per bottle instead of ₦200
questions.e: Promotion involves communicating with customers to inform, persuade or remind them about a product, and a radio jingle is a clear example of this. The other options relate to product design, place/distribution, and price respectively.
questions.p: Promotion na when business dey inform or persuade customer about product, and radio jingle na clear example of that. The other options dey talk about product design, distribution (place), and price.

questions.q: Chioma, an entrepreneur, first studies what her customers want before producing her organic honey, then designs the product, price, packaging and distribution to satisfy those needs while still making profit. This approach best illustrates the:
o: Production concept
Marketing concept
Selling concept
Product concept
questions.e: Chioma starts from customer needs before producing and arranging the full marketing mix, which is the essence of the marketing concept. The selling and production concepts focus more on pushing output or sales rather than starting from customer needs.
questions.p: Chioma first check wetin customers want before she produce and arrange product, price, packaging and distribution, na so marketing concept take be. Selling and production concepts dey focus on pushing output or sales instead of customer need first.

questions.q: A company believes that as long as it produces goods cheaply and makes them widely available, customers will automatically buy, without studying their specific needs. This belief reflects the:
o: Societal marketing concept
Marketing concept
Selling concept
Production concept
questions.e: The production concept assumes that customers mainly want cheap, widely available products, so the business focuses on efficiency and mass production rather than studying actual customer needs. This is different from the marketing concept, which starts with understanding the customer.
questions.p: Production concept na when business believe say if goods cheap and dey everywhere, customers go just buy, without the business first check wetin customer really want. E different from marketing concept wey dey start from understanding customer.

questions.q: For a bottled water company, which of the following best represents the 'product' element of its marketing mix?
o: The amount charged per bottle at retail outlets
The billboard adverts used to create awareness of the water
The actual bottle of water, including its branding, size and quality
The route trucks use to deliver water to shops in Lagos
questions.e: Product refers to the actual good or service offered, including its features such as branding, size and quality, which satisfies the customer's need. The delivery route is 'place', the amount charged is 'price', and the billboard is 'promotion'.
questions.p: Product na the actual item wey dem dey sell, with im branding, size and quality, wey dey satisfy customer need. The delivery route na 'place', the amount na 'price', and the billboard na 'promotion'.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT generally regarded as an essential element required for a valid contract?
o: An implied warranty attached to goods sold
Offer and acceptance by the parties
Legal capacity of the parties to contract
Consideration moving from the parties
questions.e: A valid contract needs offer and acceptance, consideration, capacity and intention to create legal relations. An implied warranty is a term that may apply in sale of goods, not a general requirement for forming any contract.
questions.p: For contract to dey valid, e need offer and acceptance, consideration, capacity and intention. Implied warranty na something wey dey apply for sale of goods matter, e no be general rule for all contract.

questions.q: In the law of contract, what does 'consideration' mean?
o: The price written on the receipt of a transaction
The written document used to record an agreement
Something of value given by one party in return for a promise made by the other
The person who witnesses the signing of an agreement
questions.e: Consideration is the value (money, goods, service or a promise) that each party gives in exchange for the other party's promise. Without consideration, most simple contracts cannot be enforced.
questions.p: Consideration na the value wey one party give in exchange for the promise wey the other party give. If no consideration, the ordinary contract no fit stand for court.

questions.q: Mrs Adaeze appoints Tunde to sell her goods and agrees to pay him extra commission if he personally guarantees that buyers will pay for the goods they collect on credit. What type of agent is Tunde in this arrangement?
o: A del credere agent, because he guarantees payment to the principal for extra pay
A sub-agent appointed by another agent
An agent of necessity
A universal agent
questions.e: A del credere agent receives extra commission for guaranteeing that customers he sells to on credit will pay. This is different from a general or universal agent, who simply has wide or unlimited powers without such a guarantee.
questions.p: Del credere agent na agent wey dey collect extra commission because e dey guarantee say the customer go pay the money wey e owe. Na different thing from universal agent wey just get wide power to act.

questions.q: Under the Sale of Goods Law, when goods are sold by description (for example, 'a bag of 50kg rice, Mama Gold brand'), there is an implied condition that the goods delivered must:
o: be of merchantable quality only, regardless of description
be free from any charge or encumbrance in favour of a third party
be fit for the buyer's particular purpose only
correspond with the description given at the time of sale
questions.e: When goods are sold by description, the law implies a condition that the actual goods delivered must match that description. If a trader delivers a different brand or weight from what was described, the buyer can reject the goods.
questions.p: When dem sell goods with description, na condition say the goods wey dem bring must match the description. If the trader bring different brand or weight, buyer fit reject am.

questions.q: Chidi bought a generator on hire purchase from Emeka Stores and had paid only part of the instalments. Before completing payment, Chidi sold the generator to Ngozi, who bought it in good faith believing Chidi was the owner. Under hire purchase law, who has the better title to the generator?
o: Nobody has title; the generator automatically becomes abandoned property
Emeka Stores, because ownership of goods under hire purchase remains with the seller until the final instalment is paid
Chidi, because he was in physical possession of the generator
Ngozi, because she bought in good faith and did not know about the agreement
questions.e: Under hire purchase, the hirer (Chidi) only has possession, not ownership, until all instalments are paid. Since he had no ownership, he could not transfer a better title than he had (nemo dat quod non habet), so Emeka Stores remains the rightful owner.
questions.p: For hire purchase, the person wey dey pay installment (Chidi) no be owner until e finish pay everything, na only possession e get. Since e no be owner, e no fit sell wetin e no get, so Emeka Stores still remain the real owner.

questions.q: Which of the following types of contract must generally be evidenced in writing before it can be enforced in court?
o: An oral agreement to repair a bicycle for ₦500
A contract of guarantee, where one person promises to pay another's debt if that person defaults
A verbal agreement to supply firewood to a neighbour
A contract for the sale of a bag of rice at the market
questions.e: Contracts of guarantee are special contracts that the law requires to be evidenced in writing (in line with the Statute of Frauds principle) before they can be enforced, unlike most simple everyday contracts which can be oral.
questions.p: Contract of guarantee na special one wey law say must dey written down before court go enforce am, unlike ordinary everyday contract wey fit dey verbal.

questions.q: Musa, a 16-year-old secondary school student, enters into a contract to buy a motorcycle (not a necessary item for him) on credit. Under the general law of contract, what is the status of this contract as regards Musa?
o: It is void and unenforceable against Musa, as he lacks capacity for non-necessary contracts
It is valid and fully enforceable against Musa like any adult's contract
It is binding on Musa's parents alone, since he is still a minor
It becomes valid automatically once Musa turns 25 years old
questions.e: A minor generally lacks full legal capacity to contract. Except for contracts for necessaries or beneficial contracts of service, agreements made by a minor for non-necessary items are void and cannot be enforced against the minor.
questions.p: Minor no get full capacity to enter contract. Apart from necessaries or beneficial service contract, any contract wey minor enter for non-necessary thing no valid and court no go enforce am against am.

questions.q: Which statement best explains the doctrine of 'caveat emptor' as applied in the law of sale of goods?
o: The buyer has no right to reject goods, however defective they may be
The buyer is automatically protected by an unlimited seller's warranty
The buyer must examine goods carefully before buying, since the seller is not generally liable for defects the buyer ought to have discovered
The seller must refund the buyer at any time the buyer is dissatisfied
questions.e: Caveat emptor means 'let the buyer beware'. It places the responsibility on the buyer to check goods carefully before purchase, as the seller is not automatically liable for obvious defects, except where implied conditions under the Sale of Goods Law are broken.
questions.p: Caveat emptor mean say 'make buyer dey careful'. E mean say na buyer responsibility to check the goods well before e buy, because seller no dey automatically liable for defect wey buyer suppose don see, except where the law implied conditions apply.

questions.q: What is the best definition of e-commerce as used in business studies?
o: The advertisement of goods and services on radio stations
The transportation of goods from one town to another by road
The use of a computer only to type business letters
The buying and selling of goods and services electronically, usually over the internet
questions.e: E-commerce simply means carrying out trade activities such as buying, selling and payment using electronic means like the internet. The other options describe ordinary business or transport activities that are not necessarily electronic trade.
questions.p: E-commerce na when people dey buy and sell goods or services through electronic means like internet. The other options na just normal business work wey no concern electronic trade.

questions.q: Which of the following is a genuine advantage of e-commerce to a trader?
o: It removes the need for the trader to advertise his goods
It guarantees that every customer will pay cash before the goods are delivered
It allows the trader's business to reach customers far beyond his locality at any time of the day
It removes the need for the trader to have internet access
questions.e: A major benefit of e-commerce is wider market reach, since customers anywhere can view and order goods online at any time. E-commerce actually needs internet access, cannot guarantee payment behaviour, and advertising is still important for visibility.
questions.p: Big advantage of e-commerce na say customer wey dey far from you fit still buy your goods anytime because of internet. E-commerce no fit work without internet, e no guarantee say person go pay cash, and advert still dey important.

questions.q: In e-commerce, the electronic exchange of structured business documents such as invoices and purchase orders directly between the computers of two trading partners is known as?
o: Electronic Fund Transfer (EFT) only
Automated Teller Machine (ATM) service
Point of Sale (POS) terminal transaction
Electronic Data Interchange (EDI)
questions.e: EDI specifically refers to computer-to-computer exchange of standard business documents like invoices and orders between companies. ATM, POS and EFT are related to payments and cash withdrawal, not document exchange.
questions.p: EDI na when computer dey send business paper like invoice and order go another company computer direct. ATM, POS and EFT na more about money payment, no be document exchange.

questions.q: Which of the following is a common challenge facing the growth of e-commerce in many parts of Nigeria?
o: Unreliable electricity supply and low internet access in some areas
An excess number of skilled information technology workers
Strict government control fixing the prices of all online goods
Too many commercial banks offering online payment services
questions.e: Poor power supply and limited internet coverage in some areas make it hard for both traders and customers to use e-commerce platforms steadily. Having many banks or IT workers would actually help e-commerce, and price control is not a standard Nigerian e-commerce problem.
questions.p: Light wahala and small internet for some areas na real problem for e-commerce for Nigeria. If plenty banks or IT people dey, e for even help business; government no dey fix price for everything wey dem dey sell online.

questions.q: Mr. Eze, a wholesaler, uses a computer software that automatically updates his stock records whenever goods are sold or newly received, and alerts him when it is time to reorder. This particular use of the computer in his business is best described as?
o: Electronic marketing
Inventory (stock) control
Online payment processing
Market research
questions.e: Tracking stock levels, updating records after sales or purchases, and signalling reorder points is exactly what inventory or stock control software does. It is not marketing, payment processing or research, since no advertising, money transfer or data survey is described.
questions.p: Wetin Mr Eze dey do na inventory control, because e dey track how much stock dey remain and e dey tell am when to order new goods. E no be marketing, payment or research, since no advert, money transfer or survey dey happen here.

questions.q: Which of the following statements best distinguishes Consumer-to-Consumer (C2C) e-commerce from Business-to-Consumer (B2C) e-commerce?
o: C2C involves only government agencies, while B2C involves only private companies
C2C transactions never require the internet, while B2C transactions always require the internet
C2C involves transactions directly between individual consumers, while B2C involves a registered business selling to a consumer
C2C transactions can only happen offline, while B2C transactions can only happen online
questions.e: The key difference is who the seller is: in C2C it is an ordinary individual selling to another individual, while in B2C it is a formal business selling to a consumer. The other statements wrongly limit both models to offline/online only or to government/private ownership.
questions.p: The main difference na who dey sell: for C2C na ordinary person dey sell to another person, but for B2C na real business dey sell to consumer. The other options dey wrongly limit am to offline/online or government/private only.

questions.q: Tunde wants to set up a shop that sells shoes to customers all over Nigeria through the internet and allows them to pay instantly with their bank cards. Which combination of tools would he MOST need to achieve this using e-commerce?
o: A radio jingle advertising his shop and a manual cash register at his single shop
A fax machine for orders and a postal address for customers to send letters
A printed catalogue of shoes and a local town crier announcing his prices
A company website with a shopping cart feature and a secure online payment gateway
questions.e: True e-commerce selling nationwide with instant card payment requires an online website where customers can select items (shopping cart) and pay securely online (payment gateway). Radio jingles, town criers, printed catalogues and fax machines are traditional tools that do not provide real-time online ordering and card payment.
questions.p: To really sell online well-well and collect card payment sharp-sharp, Tunde need website wit shopping cart and secure online payment gateway. Radio jingle, town crier, catalogue and fax machine na old style wey no fit give instant online order and card payment.

questions.q: Which term refers to the sum total of all internal and external factors—such as customers, government policy, culture, and competitors—that affect how a business organization operates and achieves its goals?
o: Business environment
Business ethics
Business policy
Business cycle
questions.e: The business environment is the combination of all internal and external forces that surround and influence a firm's operations. It includes things like customers, suppliers, laws, technology, and competitors.
questions.p: Business environment na all di inside and outside things wey dey affect how company dey operate, like customer, law, and competitor. E no be business cycle, policy or ethics.

questions.q: Which of the following is best classified as an INTERNAL business environment factor, rather than an external one?
o: Competitor's pricing strategy
Organizational culture
Exchange rate fluctuation
Government tax policy
questions.e: Organizational culture is created and controlled from within the business itself, unlike taxes, exchange rates, and competitor pricing which come from outside forces the firm cannot directly control.
questions.p: Organizational culture na something wey dey inside di company, so na internal factor. Tax policy, exchange rate and competitor price na external things wey dey come from outside.

questions.q: Alhaji Musa's furniture workshop in Aba had to spend extra money installing waste-treatment equipment after the state government passed a new environmental sanitation law. This situation shows the influence of which business environment factor?
o: Technological factor
Social factor
Legal factor
Natural factor
questions.e: A government law forcing businesses to meet certain standards is a legal factor, because it comes from government legislation that firms must obey, affecting how they operate.
questions.p: Na government law force am to buy waste equipment, so na legal factor dey affect am, because law na government rule wey business must obey.

questions.q: Business ethics in commerce is best described as
o: methods used by firms to advertise and promote products
strategies for maximizing profit regardless of method
government laws regulating the import and export of goods
rules and principles guiding fair and moral conduct in business dealings
questions.e: Business ethics deals with moral standards and fairness in how a business treats its workers, customers, and the public, not just profit-making or advertising methods.
questions.p: Business ethics na di moral rules wey dey guide how business dey treat worker, customer and public well-well, e no be just profit or advertisement matter.

questions.q: A bank in Enugu sponsors free medical check-ups for residents of its host community every year, even though this is not required by any law. Which is the MAIN reason businesses undertake such social responsibility activities?
o: To build goodwill and trust with the host community
To reduce the amount of tax the company pays
To avoid paying workers their full wages
To eliminate rival businesses from the market
questions.e: Companies carry out voluntary community projects mainly to create a good image, earn public trust, and maintain a healthy relationship with the people around them, which can also boost long-term business success.
questions.p: Di main reason why company dey do free medical or community project na to build good name and trust with di people around dem, even though law no force dem.

questions.q: A textile factory in Kaduna pays all its statutory taxes promptly and provides steady employment for over 400 workers, yet it releases untreated dye chemicals into a stream used by nearby farmers for irrigation, damaging their crops. This situation best shows the company fulfilling its ___ responsibility while neglecting its ___ responsibility.
o: legal; economic
economic; social
social; legal
ethical; economic
questions.e: Paying taxes and creating jobs are economic contributions to society, but harming farmers' livelihoods through pollution shows a failure in social responsibility, which is about caring for community welfare.
questions.p: Di factory dey pay tax and give people work, dat na economic responsibility, but e dey spoil farmers crop with waste, dat one na failure for social responsibility wey suppose protect community welfare.

questions.q: According to Carroll's pyramid of corporate social responsibility, which responsibility forms the FOUNDATION (base) that every business must first satisfy before pursuing the others?
o: Economic responsibility
Philanthropic responsibility
Legal responsibility
Ethical responsibility
questions.e: Carroll's pyramid places economic responsibility (being profitable and providing goods/services people need) as the base, because a business must first survive financially before it can obey laws, act ethically, or give to charity.
questions.p: For Carroll pyramid, economic responsibility (to make profit and provide goods/service) na di foundation, because business must first survive financially before e fit follow law, act ethical or do charity.

questions.q: Occupations in which people earn a living are broadly classified into three groups. These are direct production, commerce and
o: Aids to trade
Distribution of goods
Industrial production
Direct services
questions.e: Occupations are grouped into direct production (extraction and manufacture), commerce (trade and aids to trade), and direct services (such as teaching, medicine and the civil service). Direct services do not involve producing or trading goods.
questions.p: Dem dey divide work into three parts: direct production, commerce, and direct services. Direct services no dey involve to dey produce or sell goods.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of direct production, as distinct from commerce?
o: An insurance firm covering a cocoa warehouse
A bank granting loans to a cocoa exporter
A trader buying cocoa from farmers for resale
A farmer in Ondo State planting and harvesting cocoa
questions.e: Direct production involves the actual extraction or growing of raw materials or manufacture of goods, such as a farmer growing cocoa. Buying for resale, banking and insurance are trade and aids to trade, which belong to commerce.
questions.p: Direct production na wen person go farm plant cocoa or extract raw materials. To buy and sell, do banking, or insurance na commerce.

questions.q: The study of Commerce is important to a developing economy mainly because it
o: Fixes the prices of all goods produced in the country
Ensures that only government agencies distribute goods
Helps goods move efficiently from producers to the final users who need them
Prevents producers from exporting their goods abroad
questions.e: Commerce facilitates the exchange and distribution of goods and services so that they reach the people who need them, wherever they are. It does not fix prices, restrict exports or limit distribution to government alone.
questions.p: Commerce dey help goods reach people wey need dem fast. E no dey fix price or stop people make dem export goods.

questions.q: A tailor in Kano sews ready-made clothes and sells them directly to customers who walk into her shop. Mr. Eze, however, buys the same type of ready-made clothes in bulk from several tailors and resells them to retailers across three states. Which statement correctly classifies their occupations?
o: Both of them are engaged purely in direct production
The tailor is in direct production while Mr. Eze is engaged in trade
The tailor is engaged in trade while Mr. Eze is in direct production
Both of them are engaged purely in aids to trade
questions.e: The tailor manufactures the clothes herself, which is direct production, even though she also sells what she makes. Mr. Eze does not manufacture anything; he only buys and resells goods made by others, which is the trade aspect of commerce.
questions.p: Taylor dey sew cloth, na direct production be dat. Mr. Eze just dey buy and sell wetian other people don make, na trade be dat.

questions.q:
Which pair below correctly matches each person with the broad occupational group his main activity belongs to?
I. Tunde is a goldsmith who mines and refines gold himself.
II. Ngozi works as a staff nurse in a government hospital.
o: Tunde - commerce; Ngozi - direct service
Tunde - direct service; Ngozi - commerce
Tunde - commerce; Ngozi - direct production
Tunde - direct production; Ngozi - direct service
questions.e: Tunde extracts and refines a raw material himself, so his work is direct production. Ngozi offers a personal service to the public as a nurse, which falls under direct services, not trade or commerce.
questions.p: Tunde work na direct production because e dey mine gold. Ngozi work as nurse na direct service because e dey help people directly.

questions.q: A shortage of boreholes forces Mrs. Afolabi's cassava processing business in Ogun State to use river water, resulting in frequent contamination of her garri. Which problem of commerce and industry does this situation best illustrate?
o: High rate of taxation on small businesses
Low demand for processed cassava products
Poor infrastructural facilities
Inadequate capital for business expansion
questions.e: Lack of reliable water supply is an infrastructural problem, since infrastructure includes utilities like water, power and roads needed for smooth business operations. It is not about capital, taxation or demand for the product.
questions.p: Wahala of water supply na bad infrastructure because business need water and light to work well. E no consign money or tax.

questions.q: Within the scope of Commerce, 'home trade' is best described as the buying and selling of goods
o: Involving goods shipped across international waters
Carried out only by government owned companies
Entirely within the boundaries of one country
Between a Nigerian exporter and a buyer in Ghana
questions.e: Home trade, also called internal or domestic trade, refers to the exchange of goods and services entirely within one country's borders. Trade crossing national boundaries is foreign trade, not home trade.
questions.p: Home trade na when buying and selling happen inside one country alone. If e cross another country border, na foreign trade be dat.

questions.q: Okon owns a small store in Calabar. He sources garments from a wholesaler, stores them, prices them, and sells single units to walk-in customers, while also arranging for a courier firm to deliver items to customers in nearby towns. Considering the full scope of Commerce, Okon's activities combine
o: Retail trade and an aid to trade (transportation) only
Wholesale trade and manufacturing only
Banking and insurance services only
Direct production and direct service only
questions.e: Okon sells in small quantities directly to final consumers, which is retail trade, and he also uses a courier service to move goods, which is transportation, an aid to trade. He neither manufactures goods nor performs banking or insurance functions.
questions.p: Okon dey sell for him small shop, na retail trade. E also dey use courier service carry goods, na transport be dat, wey be aid to trade.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of a 'commercial service' rather than a 'direct service' within the scope of Commerce?
o: A barber cutting hair in his shop in Onitsha
A tailor sewing clothes for a customer
A doctor treating patients in a government hospital
An insurance company compensating a trader whose shop was gutted by fire
questions.e: Commercial services are those rendered by businesses as part of trade activities, such as insurance, banking and transport. Insurance compensating a trader is a commercial service because it directly supports trade, unlike personal/direct services like medical treatment or haircutting.
questions.p: Commercial services na business activities wey dey support trade like insurance and banking. Personal services like doctor or barber no be commercial service because dem no dey directly support trade.

questions.q: Which group of occupations below consists entirely of examples of 'extractive industry' under direct production?
o: Banking, insurance, and warehousing
Mining of tin, fishing in the sea, and lumbering in the forest
Baking bread, weaving cloth, and assembling cars
Farming maize, rearing poultry, and brewing beer
questions.e: Extractive industries involve taking raw materials directly from nature without changing their form, such as mining, fishing and lumbering. Baking, weaving and assembling involve manufacturing, while banking and insurance are commercial services, not extraction.
questions.p: Extractive industry na when you take raw materials direct from nature without changing dem. Mining, fishing and lumbering na correct examples, but baking and banking no be extraction.

questions.q: A manufacturer of soft drinks in Ibadan finds that his finished bottles pile up in the warehouse because there is no easy way to move them to distant markets like Sokoto and Maiduguri. Which hindrance to trade does this situation best illustrate?
o: Hindrance of time
Hindrance of risk
Hindrance of knowledge
Hindrance of place
questions.e: The hindrance of place arises when goods are produced in one location but needed in another, requiring transport to bridge the gap. Since the bottles cannot easily reach distant markets, this is a problem of place, not risk, time or knowledge.
questions.p: Hindrance of place dey happen when goods dey one place but people wey need am dey another place. Transport dey solve this problem, so the difficulty to move bottles to Sokoto na hindrance of place.

questions.q: Which of the following best explains why Commerce is classified as a tertiary occupation rather than a secondary occupation?
o: It focuses on buying and selling of goods and rendering services that support trade, rather than making goods
It is concerned only with growing crops and rearing animals for food
It involves extracting raw materials from the land and sea for direct use
It deals strictly with changing raw materials into semi-finished products
questions.e: Tertiary occupations provide services, including commerce, which links producers and consumers through trade and aids to trade. Extraction belongs to primary occupations and manufacturing belongs to secondary occupations, not commerce.
questions.p: Commerce na tertiary occupation because e dey provide services wey dey help trade flow. E no dey make goods like secondary industry or extract raw materials like primary industry.

questions.q: A furniture maker in Benin City converts wood into chairs and tables in his workshop. Under the classification of occupations, his activity falls under which broad group?
o: Direct production (primary industry)
Commerce
Direct production (secondary industry)
Aids to trade
questions.e: Direct production is divided into primary industries, which extract raw materials, and secondary industries, which manufacture goods from raw materials. Turning wood into furniture is manufacturing, so it falls under secondary industry.
questions.p: Secondary industry na where dem dey turn raw materials into finished goods. Because the man dey turn wood to furniture, e dey do manufacturing work under secondary industry.

questions.q: Mallam Sani wants to sell groundnut oil produced in Kano to buyers in Ghana. Which branch of Commerce specifically deals with this kind of transaction that crosses national borders?
o: International trade
Wholesale trade
Home trade
Retail trade
questions.e: International trade refers to the buying and selling of goods and services between people or firms in different countries. Since groundnut oil is moving from Nigeria to Ghana, this is an example of international trade, not home or retail trade.
questions.p: International trade na when you buy or sell goods between different countries. Since the groundnut oil dey go Ghana from Nigeria, na international trade be that.

questions.q: A yam farmer in Benue State harvests yams but has no reliable means of storing them for the off-season, leading to heavy losses after each harvest. This situation best illustrates which hindrance to trade that Commerce helps to solve?
o: Hindrance of exchange
Hindrance of place
Hindrance of risk
Hindrance of time
questions.e: The hindrance of time occurs when there is a gap between production and consumption, requiring storage (warehousing) to keep goods until needed. Since the farmer cannot store the yams for later sale, this is a problem of time, which warehousing as an aid to trade would resolve.
questions.p: Hindrance of time dey happen when goods no dey available when people need am. Because the farmer no get warehouse to keep the yams for later, na time problem be that.

questions.q: Which statement correctly describes the relationship between Commerce and Trade within the scope of Commerce?
o: Commerce deals only with international transactions while Trade covers only local transactions
Commerce and Trade mean exactly the same thing with no difference at all
Trade is the buying and selling of goods, while Commerce includes trade plus the aids that make trade possible
Trade is a wider term that includes Commerce and all forms of manufacturing
questions.e: Commerce is a broader term that covers trade (buying and selling) together with aids to trade such as transport, banking, insurance and warehousing, which remove hindrances to trade. Trade alone refers only to the actual exchange of goods, so it is a narrower concept than Commerce.
questions.p: Trade na just the buying and selling of goods. Commerce na bigger pass trade because e include trade plus other things like transport and banking wey dey help trade work well.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes secondary production?
o: Transporting raw cotton from the farm to the market
Converting raw materials into finished or semi-finished goods
Providing banking services to factory owners
Catching fish directly from rivers and lakes
questions.e: Secondary production involves the transformation of raw materials into finished or semi-finished goods, such as manufacturing. Fishing is primary production, while banking and transport are tertiary services.
questions.p: Secondary production na when dem dey turn raw material to finish or semi-finish goods like factory work. Fishing na primary production, while banking and transport na tertiary service.

questions.q: Which of the following is a key distinguishing feature of labour as a factor of production, compared with land and capital?
o: It can be stored indefinitely for future use
It is a human factor that can get tired and go on strike
It is completely immobile between occupations
It always earns interest as its reward
questions.e: Labour refers to human effort used in production, and because it is human, workers can get fatigued, fall ill, or embark on strikes, unlike land and capital. Interest is the reward for capital, not labour.
questions.p: Labour na human being wey dey work, so unlike land or machine, worker fit tire, sick, or go strike. Na interest dem dey pay for capital, no be labour.

questions.q: Alhaji Garba owns three hectares of farmland in Kano which he rents out to tomato farmers every planting season without working on it himself. The payment he receives for the use of this land is called ______.
o: Interest
Wages
Profit
Rent
questions.e: Rent is the reward paid to the owner of land for allowing others to use it in production. Wages reward labour, interest rewards capital, and profit rewards entrepreneurship.
questions.p: Rent na the money wey person dey collect because im allow another person use im land for work. Wages na for labour, interest na for capital, and profit na for business man.

questions.q: A small bakery in Enugu increases its output of bread from 200 loaves a day to 260 loaves a day simply by employing two more bakers, while the size of the oven and the bakery space remain unchanged. This situation best illustrates which concept?
o: Increase in fixed capital
Economies of scale
Increase in variable factor of production
Division of labour
questions.e: Labour here is a variable factor because it was increased to raise output, while the oven and space (fixed capital/land) stayed the same. This shows how varying one factor while others remain fixed can change output levels.
questions.p: Labour na variable factor here because as dem add more workers, output come increase while the oven and space remain the same. E show say changing one factor fit change how much goods you dey produce.

questions.q: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes capital from entrepreneurship as factors of production?
o: Capital is man-made wealth used to produce more wealth, while entrepreneurship organizes and bears the risk of production
Capital and entrepreneurship are the same factor with different names
Capital is a natural resource, while entrepreneurship is a reward for labour
Capital always refers to money kept in the bank, while entrepreneurship refers to land ownership
questions.e: Capital consists of man-made assets like machines and buildings used to produce further goods, whereas entrepreneurship is the factor that combines land, labour and capital, organizes production, and takes on business risk. These are distinct factors with different roles and rewards.
questions.p: Capital na things wey human make like machine to produce more goods, while entrepreneur na the person wey dey pack land, labour and capital together and carry business risk.

questions.q: A cooperative society in Benin plants oil palm trees, waits for them to mature, harvests the fruits, and sells them to a processing company. Which type of production does this activity best represent?
o: Construction production
Primary production
Tertiary production
Secondary production
questions.e: Growing and harvesting oil palm fruits directly from nature is primary production, which includes agriculture, extraction and gathering of raw materials. The processing company later carries out secondary production on the harvested fruits.
questions.p: To plant and harvest oil palm fruit directly from nature na primary production, because agriculture and farming fall inside am. Na later processing company go come do secondary production.

questions.q: A furniture workshop in Owerri currently produces 40 chairs a week using 5 carpenters and basic tools. The owner decides to combine two separate benches into one specialised assembly line, where one carpenter only cuts wood, another only joins frames, and another only polishes. Weekly output rises to 70 chairs without hiring new workers. This improvement is mainly due to ______.
o: An expansion in the size of the workshop land
A rise in the price of furniture
Specialisation and division of labour among the carpenters
An increase in the quantity of capital employed
questions.e: Output rose without adding workers, land or extra capital, showing that reorganizing tasks so each carpenter specialises in one stage of production increased efficiency and productivity. This is the benefit of division of labour and specialisation.
questions.p: Work output increase without adding more worker or tool because each carpenter face one specific work. Na the power of division of labour and specialisation be that.

questions.q: Which of the following best explains why entrepreneurship is often described as the 'organizing' factor of production rather than a passive resource like land?
o: It combines land, labour and capital, makes key decisions, and bears the uncertainty of profit or loss
It is fixed in supply and cannot be increased by training
It physically performs all the manual work in a business
It is the only factor that never requires any payment
questions.e: The entrepreneur brings together land, labour and capital, takes decisions on what and how to produce, and bears the risk of the venture succeeding or failing, earning profit as a reward. This active, risk-bearing role is different from land, which simply provides space or natural resources.
questions.p: Na entrepreneur dey join land, labour and capital together, make important decision, and carry the risk whether business go sweet or bitter. E dey different from ordinary land.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of a large-scale retail organisation that sells a wide variety of goods under one roof, usually arranged in different sections, with customers served by sales assistants in each section?
o: Co-operative wholesale society
Discount house
Itinerant trader
Department store
questions.e: A department store is a large retail outlet divided into departments selling different kinds of goods under one roof. It is a feature of large-scale retailing, unlike itinerant trading which is small-scale.
questions.p: Department store na big shop wey dem divide into different section make dem sell various goods under one roof. E dey different well well from itinerant trader wey be small-scale business.

questions.q: Mallam Garba supplies fresh tomatoes to the Mile 12 wholesale market. The wholesaler then breaks the large quantity into smaller units for different retailers. This function performed by the wholesaler is best described as:
o: Grading
Advertising
Bulk breaking
Risk bearing
questions.e: Bulk breaking means dividing large quantities bought from producers into smaller, manageable units suitable for retailers. This saves retailers from having to buy in very large quantities they cannot sell quickly.
questions.p: Bulk breaking mean say dem dey cut big quantity goods wey comot from producer into small small units wey retailers fit buy easily. Dis one dey help retailers make dem no carry excess goods wey dem no fit sell fast.

questions.q: Alhaji Musa owns a provision shop in Kano. He now wants to start supplying goods in bulk to about fifteen smaller shop owners within his area at a slightly lower price. By doing this, Alhaji Musa is beginning to perform the role of a:
o: Commission agent
Wholesaler
Retailer only
Consumer
questions.e: A wholesaler buys in bulk from producers and sells in fairly large quantities to retailers at a lower unit price than the retailer would charge the final consumer. By supplying smaller shop owners in bulk, Alhaji Musa is now acting as a wholesaler.
questions.p: Wholesaler dey buy plenty goods and sell am for big quantity to retailers. Since Alhaji Musa don start to supply other small shop owners, e don turn wholesaler be that.

questions.q: An importer in Kano wishes to bring in machinery from Germany but needs his bank to authorise a foreign bank to pay the German supplier a stated sum once shipping documents are presented. Which document should the importer's bank issue?
o: Certificate of origin
Bill of lading
Letter of hypothecation
Letter of credit
questions.e: A letter of credit is issued by the importer's bank to guarantee payment to the exporter once agreed conditions and documents are met. The other documents serve different purposes in foreign trade.
questions.p: Letter of credit na bank document wey dey guarantee say dem go pay supplier money as soon as dem bring shipping documents. E dey help build trust for international trade.

questions.q: A Nigerian exporter ships cocoa to the Netherlands and later receives payment through a bank instrument instructing the foreign buyer to pay a fixed sum on a specified date. This instrument is called a
o: bill of exchange
bill of lading
dock warrant
indent
questions.e: A bill of exchange is a written order used in foreign trade requiring the buyer to pay a stated amount at a fixed or determinable future date. It is mainly a payment instrument, unlike the other documents listed.
questions.p: Bill of exchange na written order wey dey tell buyer make e pay money for specific future date. Na correct instrument wey dem dey use for international business payment.

questions.q: In foreign trade procedure, an indent is best described as
o: a document used to claim insurance compensation
a written order sent by an importer to an agent abroad for specified goods
a certificate confirming goods meet health standards
a government levy charged on imported goods
questions.e: An indent is an order placed by a home buyer through an agent abroad, specifying the goods required and terms of purchase. The other options describe a tariff, a sanitary certificate, and an insurance claim form.
questions.p: Indent na order wey importer dey send give agent abroad to buy goods for am. E dey contain the type of goods and conditions wey dem need.

questions.q: Which of the following is a major reason why a country's balance of payments account is usually divided into current account and capital account?
o: To separate transactions in goods and services from transactions in assets and liabilities
To show only the value of smuggled goods across borders
To calculate the exchange rate of the national currency directly
To separate government revenue from private sector revenue
questions.e: The current account records trade in goods, services and income, while the capital account records financial transactions such as loans, investments and asset transfers. This separation helps economists analyse different sources of foreign exchange flows.
questions.p: Current account dey record trade for goods and services, while capital account dey record money for assets and loans. To separate dem dey help us know how foreign money dey enter and go.

questions.q: A country exported goods worth ₦450 million and imported goods worth ₦520 million in a given year, with no other visible transactions. What is the value and type of its visible trade balance for that year?
o: ₦450 million surplus
₦70 million surplus
₦970 million deficit
₦70 million deficit
questions.e: Visible trade balance equals exports minus imports: 450 million minus 520 million gives a deficit of 70 million naira. This means the country spent more on imports than it earned from exports.
questions.p: Visible trade balance na exports minus imports, wey be ₦450 million minus ₦520 million to get ₦70 million deficit. E mean say we spend pass wetл we sell.

questions.q: In international trade procedure, before goods can be shipped abroad, an exporter usually obtains a document from a recognised body certifying that the goods meet specified standards of quality. This document is known as
o: certificate of origin
warehouse warrant
certificate of inspection
consular invoice
questions.e: A certificate of inspection confirms that goods have been examined and meet required quality standards before shipment. It differs from a certificate of origin, which only states where goods were produced, and from a consular invoice, which is for customs valuation purposes.
questions.p: Certificate of inspection dey show say dem don check the goods and dem meet standard quality before shipping. E different from certificate of origin wey just dey show where dem make the goods.

questions.q: Which pair of institutions are most directly involved in verifying and clearing imported goods for an importer at a Nigerian seaport before the goods are released?
o: Nigeria Customs Service and clearing agents
Nigerian Export Promotion Council and the shipper
Nigerian Ports Authority and the manufacturer
Central Bank of Nigeria and the exporter
questions.e: The Nigeria Customs Service assesses duties and inspects goods, while licensed clearing agents handle documentation and physically clear the goods on behalf of importers. The other pairs do not perform the actual clearing function.
questions.p: Na Nigeria Customs Service dey check goods and calculate duty, while clearing agents dey help arrange di paperwork and carry di goods comot for port. Na dis two people dey work together well well for seaport.

questions.q: A manufacturer in Aba wants to find out whether there is demand for his furniture in Ghana before committing to export. The most appropriate first step in the foreign trade procedure is to
o: apply for a letter of credit immediately
obtain a bill of lading from a shipping line
sign a bill of exchange with a Ghanaian bank
conduct a market survey through trade missions or embassies
questions.e: Before any shipping or payment documents are needed, an exporter must first find out if a market exists abroad, usually through trade missions, embassies or export promotion agencies. The other options are later steps that follow after a market has been identified.
questions.p: Before you go send any market go another country, you must first find out whether people there want am through embassy or trade mission. Na after you don see market then you fit start to talk about shipping.

questions.q: A country's balance of payments records a deficit on current account but a surplus on capital account large enough to offset it. This situation best illustrates that
o: the country has stopped all visible trade
a deficit in one section can be balanced by a surplus in another section
the balance of trade and balance of payments mean the same thing
the overall balance of payments must always be in deficit
questions.e: The balance of payments is made up of several accounts (current, capital, financial) and a shortfall in one can be covered by a surplus in another, keeping the overall balance in equilibrium. This shows why the accounts are split into sections rather than treated as one single figure.
questions.p: Balance of payments get different accounts like current and capital account. If one side get shortage, another side surplus fit cover am make everything balance.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes the role of a freight forwarder in foreign trade procedure?
o: Issuing import licences to traders
Fixing the exchange rate between the naira and foreign currencies
Arranging transportation and documentation for goods on behalf of exporters or importers
Lending foreign currency to importers
questions.e: A freight forwarder organises the movement of goods, including booking shipping space and preparing shipping documents, acting as an agent for the trader. Lending money, fixing exchange rates and issuing licences are not functions of a freight forwarder.
questions.p: Freight forwarder na di person wey dey arrange transport and all di document wey goods need for export or import. Dem no dey give loan or fix exchange rate.

questions.q: A Nigerian trading company received a document from its overseas supplier showing the quantity, price and description of goods already dispatched, which it will use to check against the goods received and to process payment. This document is called a
o: pro-forma invoice
commercial invoice
certificate of origin
indent
questions.e: A commercial invoice is sent after goods have been dispatched and gives full details of quantity, price and description, serving as a demand for payment and a basis for checking goods received. A pro-forma invoice is only a quotation sent before the order is confirmed.
questions.p: Commercial invoice na di paper wey supplier go send after dem don send di goods, showing price and quantity wey person go use pay. Pro-forma invoice na just quotation before order happen.

questions.q: A country recorded the following for one year: visible exports ₦620 million, visible imports ₦580 million, invisible exports ₦90 million and invisible imports ₦150 million. What is the balance on current account?
o: ₦40 million surplus
₦60 million surplus
₦20 million deficit
₦40 million deficit
questions.e: Balance of trade = 620 - 580 = 40 million surplus. Invisible balance = 90 - 150 = -60 million. Current account balance = 40 + (-60) = -20 million, which is a 20 million deficit.
questions.p: Visible trade balance na 620 minus 580 wey be 40 million surplus, while invisible trade balance na 90 minus 150 wey be 60 million deficit. When you add dem together, you go get 20 million deficit for current account.

questions.q: In foreign trade documentation, the main purpose of a certificate of insurance accompanying an export consignment is to
o: authorise the shipping line to load the goods on board
confirm that the goods have been inspected by customs
show the country where the goods were manufactured
provide evidence that the goods are covered against loss or damage in transit
questions.e: A certificate of insurance shows that the goods being shipped are covered against risks such as damage, loss or theft while in transit, giving the buyer assurance of compensation if something goes wrong. It has nothing to do with customs inspection, origin or loading authorisation.
questions.p: Certificate of insurance na evidence say if anything happen to di goods like loss or damage for road or sea, dem go pay you back. E no concern customs inspection at all.

questions.q: A trader buys goods on credit and later returns damaged items to the supplier. Which document will the supplier issue to the trader to correct the original invoice?
o: Credit note
Statement of account
Debit note
Proforma invoice
questions.e: A credit note is issued by a seller to reduce the amount a buyer owes, usually because of returned or damaged goods. It corrects the invoice in favour of the buyer.
questions.p: Na credit note dem dey use reduce the money wey buyer suppose pay when e return bad goods. E dey correct the invoice for buyer favor.

questions.q: Under which international trade term does the buyer bear the cost of marine insurance and freight from the port of shipment to the port of destination, since the quoted price only covers the goods up to the ship's rail?
o: Carriage paid
Ex-works
FOB
CIF
questions.e: Under FOB, the seller's responsibility ends once goods are loaded on board the ship, so the buyer pays for freight and insurance afterwards. This differs from CIF, where the seller covers freight and insurance.
questions.p: Under FOB, once dem load goods for ship, seller work don finish. Na buyer con dey pay for freight and insurance.

questions.q: Mallam Bello buys goods worth ₦80,000 (list price) from a distributor who grants him a 15% trade discount. What amount will Mallam Bello pay to the distributor?
questions.e: Trade discount is 15% of 80,000, which is 12,000. Subtracting this from the list price gives 80,000 - 12,000 = 68,000, the amount payable.
questions.p: Trade discount na 15% of ₦80,000, wey be ₦12,000. When you minus am from the list price, you go get ₦68,000 as the money to pay.

questions.q: An invoice shows goods valued at ₦60,000 after a trade discount has already been deducted. The supplier further offers a 4% cash discount for payment within 14 days. If Mrs. Adaeze pays within the period, how much does she pay?
questions.e: Cash discount is 4% of 60,000, which is 2,400. Subtracting this from 60,000 gives 57,600, the amount paid for prompt settlement.
questions.p: Cash discount na 4% of ₦60,000, wey be ₦2,400. If you minus am from ₦60,000, the remaining money wey person go pay na ₦57,600.

questions.q: A supplier's list price for goods is ₦120,000. He allows a trade discount of 10% and, on the net amount after this discount, a further cash discount of 5% for payment within 7 days. If Mr. Okon pays within 7 days, how much does he pay?
questions.e: Trade discount of 10% on 120,000 leaves 108,000. Cash discount of 5% is then applied to 108,000, giving 5,400 off, so the final payment is 108,000 - 5,400 = 102,600.
questions.p: Trade discount of 10% on ₦120,000 go leave ₦108,000. If you come remove 5% cash discount from ₦108,000, the final money wey e go pay na ₦102,600.

questions.q: Which of the following best explains why trade discount, unlike cash discount, does not appear as a separate figure in the trader's account books?
o: It is deducted before the invoice is prepared, so only the net price is recorded
It is recorded as an expense in the profit and loss account
It is treated as a loan to the buyer
It is given only to cash customers who pay immediately
questions.e: Trade discount is subtracted from the list price before the invoice price is fixed, so the books only show the net figure. Cash discount, however, is recorded separately because it depends on when payment is made.
questions.p: Dem dey remove trade discount before dem write invoice, na that net price dem dey record for book. Cash discount na separate thing because e dey depend on when person pay.

questions.q: A Lagos exporter quotes a price of ₦450,000 to a foreign buyer under CIF terms. Which of these costs is the exporter responsible for under this quotation?
o: Cost of goods and insurance only, excluding freight charges
Cost of goods, freight and insurance up to the destination port
Cost of goods, freight, insurance and import duties at destination
Cost of goods only, with the buyer arranging all transport
questions.e: CIF stands for Cost, Insurance and Freight, meaning the seller's quoted price already covers the goods, their insurance and freight to the destination port. Import duties are not part of CIF and remain the buyer's responsibility.
questions.p: CIF mean Cost, Insurance and Freight, so the price wey seller give don cover goods, insurance and transport go reach destination port. Import duty no join.

questions.q: Which of the following is the MOST appropriate medium of advertising for a new brand of biscuit targeted at the entire literate and non-literate population across Nigeria?
o: Billboard only
Direct mail
Trade journal
Television
questions.e: Television combines sound and pictures, reaching both literate and non-literate audiences across a wide area. Trade journals and direct mail are limited to specific literate groups, while billboards alone cover only fixed locations.
questions.p: Television dey use sound and picture, so e dey reach both people wey sabi book and the ones wey no sabi book across everywhere. Other ones like trade journal and direct mail na only few people wey sabi book dey see them, and billboard dey stay one place.

questions.q: A manufacturer of detergent attaches a small plastic bucket as a free gift to every carton bought by wholesalers during a festive period. This method of boosting sales is best described as:
o: Publicity
Public relations
Premium offer
Institutional advertising
questions.e: A premium offer is a sales promotion technique where a free extra item is given to encourage buyers to purchase a product. It is not advertising, publicity or public relations because it involves a direct, tangible incentive attached to the purchase.
questions.p: Premium offer na sales promotion style where dem dey give free item join so that buyers go buy product. E no be advertising or publicity because na direct gift dem attach to the purchase.

questions.q: Which of these best explains why outdoor advertising such as billboards is generally cheaper per exposure than television advertising for a Nigerian company?
o: Billboards are only used in rural areas where costs are lower
Billboards have a fixed location and are viewed repeatedly over a long period without extra charge
Television stations do not charge for advertising slots
Billboards require no artwork or design cost
questions.e: Once a billboard is erected and paid for, it continues to be seen by passers-by repeatedly over weeks or months at no extra cost, spreading the cost per view. Television, in contrast, charges for each time slot the advert is aired.
questions.p: Once dem erect billboard and pay for am, people go dey see am every time over weeks or months without extra charge, making the cost per view cheap. Television dey charge money anytime dem play the advert.

questions.q: A new entrant into the Nigerian soft drink market spends heavily on television and radio adverts for six months purely to make consumers aware that the brand exists, without mentioning price or where to buy it. This type of advertising is called:
o: Pioneering advertising
Competitive advertising
Reminder advertising
Cooperative advertising
questions.e: Pioneering advertising is used to introduce a new product and create basic awareness and demand in the market. Competitive advertising compares brands, reminder advertising sustains existing demand, and cooperative advertising is jointly funded by manufacturer and retailer.
questions.p: Pioneering advertising naim dem dey use introduce new product so people go know say e dey market. E no talk about price or where to buy am, na just to create awareness.

questions.q: Which of the following is a major limitation of using newspapers as an advertising medium in many Nigerian rural communities?
o: Newspapers are more expensive than television adverts
Newspapers are too colourful and attractive
Newspaper adverts cannot carry pictures
High rate of illiteracy and low newspaper circulation in such areas
questions.e: Many rural dwellers cannot read, and newspapers may not even be readily available there, so the message fails to reach them. This makes newspapers less effective compared with media like radio that do not require literacy.
questions.p: For village areas, many people no fit read book and newspapers no even dey reach there well. This one make newspaper advertising no good for village like radio.

questions.q: A supermarket in Enugu reduces the price of a tin of milk from ₦1,200 to ₦1,000 for one week only, clearly labelled 'Special Offer', to clear excess stock. This practice is an example of:
o: Price discrimination
Dumping
Sales promotion through price reduction
Advertising
questions.e: A temporary price cut designed to encourage quick buying and clear stock is a classic sales promotion technique. It is not advertising, which focuses on communication rather than a direct price incentive, and it is not dumping or discrimination since there is no selling below cost in a foreign market or unfair customer targeting.
questions.p: When supermarket reduce price small time to sell old goods, na sales promotion through price reduction. E no be ordinary advertising because price drop dey involved.

questions.q: Two rival bread companies, Sunrise Bread and Daybreak Bread, both spend large sums on advertising mainly to protect their existing market share from each other rather than to grow the total market for bread. An economist analysing this situation would most likely argue that such advertising:
o: Increases total industry demand by informing new consumers
Mainly redistributes existing demand between the two firms, adding to cost without much new market growth
Eliminates the need for product pricing strategy entirely
Has no cost implication for either company
questions.e: When rival firms in a mature market advertise mainly against each other, much of the spending simply shifts customers between brands instead of expanding the overall market, raising costs for both without raising total sales much.
