This is a common criticism of competitive advertising in such industries.
questions.p: If two companies dey fight market with advert, dem just dey share the same customers among themselves instead of bringing new buyers. E dey add cost to them without growing the market big.

questions.q: A cosmetics firm in Lagos budgets ₦2,000,000 for a sales promotion campaign. It plans to spend 40% on free product samples, 25% on point-of-sale displays in shops, and the remainder on a 'buy two get one free' offer. How much naira will be spent on the 'buy two get one free' offer?
questions.e: Samples take 40% (₦800,000) and displays take 25% (₦500,000), totalling 65% or ₦1,300,000. The remainder, 35% of ₦2,000,000, is ₦700,000, which goes to the buy-two-get-one-free offer.
questions.p: If samples take 40 percent and displays take 25 percent, everything na 65 percent which be ₦1,300,000. The remaining 35 percent wey remain for the ₦2,000,000 na ₦700,000 for the buy two get one free offer.

questions.q: Which type of bank mainly mobilizes small savings from petty traders, farmers and other low-income earners in rural and semi-urban communities, often granting small loans to members?
o: Development bank
Central bank
Merchant bank
Community/microfinance bank
questions.e: Community and microfinance banks focus on collecting small deposits and giving small loans to low-income people in local communities. Merchant, central and development banks serve different, larger-scale purposes.
questions.p: Na microfinance bank dem dey use help small business people and farmers for village. Dem dey collect small-small money and give dem loan to take grow dia business.

questions.q: Alhaji Garba wants to deposit ₦200,000 with a bank for 9 months at an agreed fixed interest rate, with the understanding that he will not withdraw the money before the end of the period. Which type of bank account is most suitable for him?
o: Fixed deposit account
Current account
Domiciliary account
Savings account
questions.e: A fixed deposit account locks money for an agreed period at a fixed interest rate, exactly matching Alhaji Garba's plan. Current and savings accounts allow more flexible withdrawals, while a domiciliary account is for foreign currency.
questions.p: Fixed deposit account na di correct one because di money go stay for bank for specific time. You no fit touch am until di time finish, and dem go pay you interest.

questions.q: A commercial bank keeps a certain fraction of its total deposits as cash reserve and lends out the rest to borrowers. If the bank has ₦4,000,000 in total deposits and the Central Bank's required reserve ratio is 15%, how much can the bank legally give out as loans?
questions.e: Reserve amount is 15% of 4,000,000, which is 600,000. The remaining amount available for loans is 4,000,000 minus 600,000, giving 3,400,000.
questions.p: If you calculate 15% of 4,000,000, e go give you 600,000 as reserve. So, di bank go minus that 600,000 from di 4,000,000, wey come leave 3,400,000 for loan.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes 'bank draft' as a banking service?
o: An instrument issued by a bank, drawn on itself, guaranteeing payment to a named person
A loan given to a trader for business expansion
An agreement allowing a customer to overdraw their account
A record showing all transactions on a customer's account
questions.e: A bank draft is issued and guaranteed by the bank itself, making it more secure than an ordinary cheque, and is often used for large or official payments. The other options describe loans, statements, and overdrafts, which are different services.
questions.p: Bank draft na paper wey bank write by demsef to promise say dem go pay person. E dey very safe pass ordinary cheque because na di bank get di money.

questions.q: Which of these is a major function of the Central Bank of Nigeria that distinguishes it from commercial banks?
o: Issuing cheque books to private business customers
Accepting current account deposits from the general public
Acting as banker and financial adviser to the Federal Government
Granting personal loans to individual customers
questions.e: The Central Bank serves as banker, adviser and manager of government finances and foreign reserves, a role commercial banks do not perform. Commercial banks, not the Central Bank, deal directly with the public through deposits, loans and cheque books.
questions.p: Central Bank na di bank for government, dem dey advise dem and keep dia money. Commercial banks dey deal with ordinary people like you and me, but Central Bank no dey do dat one.

questions.q: Mrs Adeyemi issued a cheque for ₦80,000 to a supplier, but her account balance was only ₦55,000 at the time the cheque was presented. What is the most likely action the bank will take?
o: Automatically convert the cheque into a fixed deposit
Pay the full ₦80,000 and later recover the shortfall from the supplier
Pay ₦55,000 and ask the supplier to accept the balance later
Dishonour the cheque and mark it 'refer to drawer'
questions.e: Since the account lacks sufficient funds to cover the full cheque amount, the bank will dishonour it and stamp it 'refer to drawer', meaning the drawer should be contacted. Banks do not partially pay cheques or convert them into deposits without the customer's instruction.
questions.p: If money no reach for account, bank no go pay di cheque. Dem go just mark am 'refer to drawer' make you go settle di person wey you give di cheque.

questions.q: A bank in Lagos agrees to finance a trader's import of goods from China by guaranteeing payment to the foreign seller once shipping documents are presented, while the trader repays the bank later. This banking service is known as
o: Bank reconciliation
Letter of credit
Standing order
Direct debit
questions.e: A letter of credit is a guarantee of payment issued by a bank on behalf of a buyer, used mainly in international trade to assure the foreign seller of payment. Standing orders and direct debits deal with regular domestic payments, while reconciliation is an accounting check, not a payment guarantee.
questions.p: Letter of credit na wetin bank dey use guarantee payment for international trade. E dey make di person wey dey sell goods for outside country trust say e go collect him money.

questions.q: Before standard currency emerged, early traders used certain commodities such as cowrie shells, salt, and gold dust as a medium of exchange. This stage in the evolution of money is best described as the use of what?
o: Fiat money
Near money
Representative money
Commodity money
questions.e: Commodity money refers to items with intrinsic value, like cowrie shells or salt, that were accepted in exchange before coins and notes were invented. This came before paper money and electronic money.
questions.p: Commodity money na those things wey get value for body like cowrie and salt wey people dey use exchange before paper money come. E happen before paper money and electronic money.

questions.q: Mrs Adaeze borrowed ₦80,000 from a cooperative society and agreed to repay ₦80,000 plus interest after six months. Which function of money allows the amount owed to be fixed and recorded this way?
o: Standard for deferred payment
Measure of value
Store of value
Medium of exchange
questions.e: Money acts as a standard for deferred payment when debts or future obligations are expressed in fixed monetary terms, as with Mrs Adaeze's loan. This is different from simply measuring the value of goods today.
questions.p: Money dey act as standard for deferred payment when person borrow debt and fix am make e pay later with specific amount. Na dis one make Mrs Adaeze fit owe money and agree how e go repay am.

questions.q: A trader keeps part of his profit as cash at home instead of spending it immediately, planning to use it to restock his shop next month. Which function of money is he making use of?
o: Unit of account
Standard for deferred payment
Store of value
Medium of exchange
questions.e: Money serves as a store of value when it is kept for future use without losing its purchasing power immediately. The trader is saving cash rather than exchanging it or measuring value with it.
questions.p: Money dey serve as store of value when person keep am for future use instead of spending am sharp sharp. Di trader dey save di cash make e fit use am restock him shop next month.

questions.q: If ordinary leaves or sand were used as money, people would reject them as payment because they can be picked up freely with little effort. This shows that for an item to function well as money, it must possess which quality?
o: Durability
Scarcity
Portability
Divisibility
questions.e: Money must be relatively scarce so that it retains value; items that are too freely available, like leaves or sand, cannot serve as money. Scarcity ensures people cannot simply produce their own supply.
questions.p: Money must scarce small make e fit retain value; if ordinary sand or leaf be money, nobody go want accept am. Scarcity dey make sure say people no just wake up dey produce their own money anyhow.

questions.q: A trader in Onitsha market refuses to accept a badly torn and faded ₦1000 note, insisting it be exchanged at the bank first before he can use it in business. This situation best illustrates a weakness related to which quality of money?
o: Uniformity
Elasticity of supply
Durability
Malleability
questions.e: Durability requires money to withstand wear and tear and remain fit for repeated use; a torn, faded note fails this test and becomes hard to use in transactions. This is why the trader rejects it despite its face value.
questions.p: Durability mean say money suppose strong make e no tear quick quick for hand. As di ₦1000 note tear and fade, e don lose that durability quality, na why di trader reject am.

questions.q: In comparing the evolution of money, which of the following correctly arranges the stages from EARLIEST to MOST RECENT?
o: Trade by barter, metallic coins, paper currency, electronic money
Metallic coins, electronic money, trade by barter, paper currency
Electronic money, paper currency, metallic coins, trade by barter
Paper currency, trade by barter, electronic money, metallic coins
questions.e: Historically, people first practised trade by barter, then moved to metallic coins, followed by paper currency, and finally modern electronic money such as bank transfers and cards. This sequence reflects the true historical development of exchange systems.
questions.p: Na trade by barter start before people come begin use metallic coins, then paper currency enter, and now we dey use electronic money. Dis na di correct way money take evolve reach where we dey today.

questions.q: A civil servant wants to buy a used generator from a mechanic, but the mechanic does not need any of the services the civil servant can offer. This situation best illustrates which major weakness of the barter system?
o: Indivisibility of goods for exchange
Lack of a common measure of value
Absence of a store of value
Lack of double coincidence of wants
questions.e: Barter requires that each party wants exactly what the other is offering. Since the mechanic has no need for the civil servant's services, there is no double coincidence of wants, so the exchange cannot take place.
questions.p: Barter system dey hard because both people must want wetin each person get. Since the mechanic no need the civil servant work, the exchange no fit happen.

questions.q: A bank grants Mrs Bello a loan of ₦200,000 to be repaid in full after one year with interest. The agreement to repay a fixed naira amount in the future, rather than goods, best illustrates which function of money?
o: Store of value
Standard for deferred payment
Measure of value
Medium of exchange
questions.e: Money allows debts and future obligations to be stated and settled in fixed monetary terms. Because the loan agreement fixes a naira amount to be repaid later, money is acting as a standard for deferred payment.
questions.p: Money dey allow people to settle debt for future time. Because the loan agreement fix the naira amount to pay back later, money dey act as standard for deferred payment.

questions.q: Chidinma sells her smartphone for ₦60,000 cash but does not spend it immediately; instead she keeps it in a safe for three months before using it to pay her brother's school fees. Which function of money is being demonstrated by her keeping the cash unspent?
o: Store of value
Medium of exchange
Standard for deferred payment
Unit of account
questions.e: Money that is held without losing its purchasing power over time, ready to be used later, is performing the store of value function. Chidinma is simply saving the cash for future use rather than exchanging it or measuring worth.
questions.p: When you keep money for long time without e lose value, you dey use am as store of value. Chidinma just dey save the cash so she go fit use am later.

questions.q: Why is gold, rather than perishable farm produce like tomatoes, considered more suitable to serve as a form of money in a trading community?
o: Gold can be divided into smaller pieces without losing value
Gold is produced in larger quantities than tomatoes
Gold does not decay or deteriorate over a long period
Gold is more acceptable to foreign traders only
questions.e: A good form of money must be durable so that it can be stored and used over time without spoiling. Tomatoes rot quickly and lose value, while gold remains unchanged for very long periods, making it more suitable as money.
questions.p: Money suppose dey durable so e no go spoil quick. Tomato go rot fast, but gold go stay for long time without spoil, so e better pass tomato.

questions.q: Which of the following best explains why government-issued currency notes are generally accepted as money throughout a country, unlike privately printed vouchers?
o: They are made from specially imported paper
They are produced in unlimited quantities by banks
They can be exchanged only within one state
They are backed by legal tender status granted by the government
questions.e: Legal tender status means the law compels citizens to accept the currency in settlement of debts, giving it general acceptability nationwide. Private vouchers lack this legal backing, so sellers may refuse them.
questions.p: Legal tender mean say law talk say everybody must accept the money for payment. Because government back the currency, people must collect am, unlike private paper.

questions.q: A trader in Kano is given the choice between accepting payment in a foreign currency that fluctuates sharply in value every week, or in the local naira which has been relatively steady. If the trader prefers the naira for this reason, which quality of money is he most concerned about?
o: Cognisability
Stability of value
Portability
Homogeneity
questions.e: Stability of value means money should keep a fairly constant purchasing power over time. The trader avoids the fluctuating foreign currency because its unstable value makes it unreliable for pricing and saving.
questions.p: Stability of value mean say money purchasing power no suppose dey jump up and down. The trader no want the foreign currency because the value dey change too much.

questions.q: A market woman weighs out and sells gold dust to buyers in small quantities to match the exact value of goods being bought, without any piece losing its worth when cut. This practice best illustrates which quality that money must possess?
o: Acceptability
Scarcity
Divisibility
Durability
questions.e: Divisibility means money can be broken into smaller units without losing its total value, which allows exact amounts to be paid for goods of different prices. Cutting the gold dust into smaller quantities for transactions shows this quality.
questions.p: Divisibility mean say you fit cut money into small-small pieces without e lose value. The woman fit cut the gold dust to match the price of wetin she dey sell.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the generally recognised classes of insurance practised in Nigeria?
o: Fire insurance
Marine insurance
Life assurance
Speculative insurance
questions.e: Insurance covers pure risk where loss is possible but not certain, so it cannot cover speculative risk where there is a chance of gain or loss. Life, marine and fire insurance are all standard recognised classes.
questions.p: Insurance dey cover pure risk wey fit cause loss but no fit give gain. Speculative risk no be insurance matter because gain fit dey. Na why dem no dey recognise speculative insurance.

questions.q: Mr Bello's shop was destroyed by flood. Before the insurance company pays his claim, it sends an assessor to determine the exact cause and amount of loss. This process is called:
o: Loss assessment
Subrogation
Underwriting
Premium rating
questions.e: Loss assessment is the process of investigating and determining the actual value of a claim before payment is made. Underwriting relates to accepting risk, while subrogation concerns recovering losses from a third party.
questions.p: Loss assessment na di work wey dem dey do to check how much loss happen before dem pay claim. Underwriting na to accept risk, no be to check loss. Na loss assessment be di correct name for wetin dem do for Mr Bello shop.

questions.q: Which type of life policy pays a benefit to the insured's beneficiaries if death occurs within a stated period, but pays nothing if the insured survives beyond that period?
o: Whole life policy
Annuity policy
Endowment policy
Term assurance policy
questions.e: Term assurance only pays out if death occurs within the agreed period and has no maturity value if the person survives. Whole life and endowment policies, unlike term assurance, guarantee a payout eventually or at maturity.
questions.p: Term assurance na policy wey only pay if person die within di time wey dem agree. If di person survive pass dat time, dem no go pay anything. E different from whole life or endowment policy wey get maturity value.

questions.q: A bonded warehouse is best described as a warehouse where:
o: Perishable goods are kept under refrigeration
Goods are stored temporarily and import duty is paid later before release
Farmers store produce rent-free until harvest season ends
Goods are stored only for export without any customs control
questions.e: A bonded warehouse allows traders to keep imported goods under customs control until duty is eventually paid before the goods are released for sale.
questions.p: Bonded warehouse na place where importers dey keep dia goods under customs watch. Dem no dey pay duty sharp sharp until dem wan carry di goods go market.

questions.q: Which of the following best explains why railway transport is generally more suitable than road transport for moving heavy bulk cargo like groundnuts over very long distances?
o: Railway wagons can deliver goods directly to any village without extra handling
Railway tracks are cheaper to construct than roads
Railway transport carries large quantities at lower cost per tonne over long distances
Railway transport is faster over short distances within a city
questions.e: Rail transport benefits from economies of scale, so moving heavy bulky goods over long distances costs less per tonne than road transport, even though it needs further handling for final delivery.
questions.p: Train transport good for heavy goods like groundnut because e dey carry plenty load at once. E dey cost cheaper per tonne to travel long distance pass motor transport.

questions.q: Which of these is a genuine disadvantage of water (sea) transport in international trade?
o: It is usually slower than road or air transport, so delivery takes longer
It cannot be used to transport liquids such as crude oil
It cannot carry bulky or heavy goods at all
It is more expensive per tonne than air transport for all goods
questions.e: Sea transport, though cheap for bulky cargo, moves slowly compared with road or air transport, which can delay delivery of goods, especially perishables.
questions.p: Ship transport dey carry heavy load well well, but e dey slow die. Because e dey take time, goods fit late to reach house, especially perishable things.

questions.q: One key function of warehousing, besides storage, is price stabilisation. This means warehousing helps to:
o: Eliminate the need for insurance on stored goods
Reduce excess supply at harvest and release goods gradually to prevent sharp price swings
Increase the selling price of goods immediately after production
Fix government prices for all goods in the market permanently
questions.e: By storing surplus produce after harvest and releasing it bit by bit when demand rises, warehousing helps smooth out price fluctuations between periods of glut and scarcity.
questions.p: Warehousing dey help stabilise price because e go hide excess goods during harvest time. When famine or demand come high, dem go begin release am small small so price no go scatter.

questions.q: A manufacturing company that owns and operates its own warehouse to store its finished goods before distribution is using a:
o: Private warehouse
Public warehouse
Bonded warehouse
Co-operative warehouse
questions.e: A private warehouse is owned and used by a single firm solely for storing its own goods, unlike public warehouses which serve many different users.
questions.p: Private warehouse naim be say na only dat particular company own di house and dey use am keep dia own goods. Na different thing from public warehouse wey anybody fit rent.

questions.q: Which of the following is a major advantage of air transport over other modes when exporting fresh flowers from Nigeria to Europe?
o: It can carry extremely heavy and bulky loads more cheaply than ships
It requires no special packaging or handling procedures
It has the lowest cost per kilogram for all cargo types
It delivers perishable goods quickly, reducing spoilage before sale
questions.e: Air transport is fast, so perishable goods like fresh flowers reach distant markets quickly before they spoil, even though it costs more than sea transport for bulky goods.
questions.p: Aero-plane fast well well, na why dem dey use am carry fresh flowers from Naija go Europe. E dey make perishable goods reach market sharp sharp before e spoil, even though freight cost high.

questions.q: Which of the following is a major disadvantage of using oral communication (such as telephone calls) in business transactions?
o: It can reach a large number of people at once
It is always more expensive than written communication
It provides no permanent record for future reference
It allows immediate feedback from the receiver
questions.e: Oral messages are spoken and not written down, so there is usually no permanent record to refer to later if a dispute arises. Immediate feedback is actually an advantage, not a disadvantage.
questions.p: Oral message no dey carry permanent record wey person go use later if wahala come. To get quick answer na advantage, no be disadvantage.

questions.q: Alhaji Musa in Kaduna wants to pay his supplier in Benin City through the post office without sending physical cash, and he wants the supplier to be able to cash it at any post office near him. Which postal facility best suits this need?
o: Postal order
Registered letter
Private mail bag
Speed post
questions.e: A postal order is a document bought at a post office for a fixed sum of money, which can be sent and cashed at any post office, making it suitable for transferring money safely without sending cash. Registered letter only protects letters, not direct money transfer in this form.
questions.p: Postal order na correct paper wey person fit buy for post office make another person go cash am anywhere safely. Registered letter just dey protect letter, no be to send money like dat.

questions.q: Which of the following is a type of partner who takes part in the day-to-day management of the business and is also liable for its debts without limit?
o: Sleeping partner
Limited partner
Nominal partner
Active partner
questions.e: An active partner contributes capital, participates actively in management and bears unlimited liability. A sleeping partner only invests capital without taking part in management, while a nominal partner merely lends his name.
questions.p: Active partner dey put money, dey manage business everyday, and e get unlimited liability. Sleeping partner no dey manage, and nominal partner na just name e dey lend.

questions.q: Which of the following is a major disadvantage common to both sole proprietorship and ordinary partnership?
o: Separate legal existence from owners
Transfer of shares on the stock exchange
Difficulty in raising large capital
Continuity after the death of an owner
questions.e: Both business units rely mainly on the owners' personal savings and limited borrowing, making it hard to raise large capital compared to companies. The other options describe features of limited liability companies, not sole proprietorships or partnerships.
questions.p: Sole proprietorship and partnership dey struggle to get big money because dem dey rely on personal savings. Unlike companies, dem no get easy way to raise large capital.

questions.q: Which of these is a valid legal way by which a partnership can be dissolved?
o: Appointment of a managing director by shareholders
Death, bankruptcy or withdrawal of a partner
Conversion of ordinary shares into preference shares
Transfer of partnership shares to the stock exchange
questions.e: A partnership, unlike a company, is easily dissolved by events such as the death, bankruptcy or retirement of any partner because it lacks separate legal existence. The other options relate to company administration, not partnerships.
questions.p: Partnership no get separate legal existence, so if one partner die, go bankrupt, or commot, the business fit dissolve. Other options na things wey concern company, no be partnership.

questions.q: A sole trader wants to expand his business but is unwilling to share ownership and control with anyone else. Based on this concern, which source of additional finance would be most suitable for him?
o: Converting the business into a public company
Issuing ordinary shares to the public
Admitting a new partner
Obtaining a bank loan
questions.e: A bank loan allows the sole trader to raise funds while keeping full ownership and control of the business. Admitting a partner, issuing shares, or forming a public company would all involve sharing ownership or control with others.
questions.p: If the man no wan share control, bank loan na the best way to get money. If e take partner or sell shares, e go lose part of the control.

questions.q: Mr. Obi and Mr. Danladi are partners in a transport business. Mr. Obi contributed ₦400,000 while Mr. Danladi contributed ₦600,000. Their deed is silent on profit sharing. At the end of the year, the business made a profit of ₦200,000. Under the Partnership Act, how should the profit be shared?
o: ₦100,000 to each partner equally
All the profit goes to Mr. Danladi since he contributed more capital
₦60,000 to Mr. Obi and ₦140,000 to Mr. Danladi
₦80,000 to Mr. Obi and ₦120,000 to Mr. Danladi, based on capital ratio
questions.e: Where a partnership deed is silent on profit sharing, the Partnership Act states that profits and losses should be shared equally among partners regardless of capital contributed. So ₦200,000 divided equally gives ₦100,000 each.
questions.p: If partnership deed no talk how dem go share profit, law talk say make dem share am equal. So, even if one person put more money, dem go still share the ₦200,000 fifty-fifty.

questions.q: A private limited liability company registered under the Companies and Allied Matters Act must have its membership restricted to a maximum of:
o: 20 members
50 members
100 members
Unlimited members
questions.e: Under Nigerian company law, a private limited company is restricted to a maximum of 50 members, excluding current employees who are also members. This distinguishes it from a public company which can have unlimited members.
questions.p: Under Naija company law, private limited company must not pass 50 members, not counting workers wey join body. Dem dey do dis one to separate am from public company wey fit get plenty members.

questions.q: Before a joint stock company can legally commence business as a corporate body, it must first obtain which document from the Corporate Affairs Commission?
o: Trading licence from the local government
Tax clearance certificate
Certificate of incorporation
Memorandum of understanding only
questions.e: The certificate of incorporation is issued after registration and gives the company its legal existence as a separate entity. Without it, the company cannot sue, be sued, or own property in its own name.
questions.p: Na certificate of incorporation dem dey give company after registration make e get legal power to stand alone. Without dis paper, company no fit sue person, court no fit sue am, nor make e own property for im own name.

questions.q: Chidi wants to start a business that will allow him to raise large capital by selling shares to the general public through the stock exchange. Which type of business unit should he form?
o: Cooperative society
Public limited liability company
Sole proprietorship
Private limited liability company
questions.e: A public limited liability company can advertise its shares and sell them to the general public through the stock exchange, allowing it to raise large amounts of capital. Private companies and cooperatives cannot offer shares to the public in this way.
questions.p: Public limited liability company na im be the correct choice because dem get power to sell shares to anybody for stock exchange to gather big money. Private companies and cooperatives no fit sell shares like dat to public.

questions.q: A cooperative society differs from a joint stock company mainly in the way profit is shared because cooperative surplus is usually distributed based on:
o: The length of time a member has been registered
Equal sharing regardless of any participation
The number of shares a member bought
The volume of business a member transacted with the society
questions.e: In cooperative societies, surplus (dividend) is shared mainly according to the amount of patronage or business each member transacted with the society, not according to capital invested. This reflects the cooperative principle of mutual self-help rather than capital reward.
questions.p: For cooperative society, dem dey share surplus based on how much business person do with dem, and not how much money im put. Na im make cooperative different from ordinary joint stock company.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes a public enterprise as used in business studies?
o: A business formed by a group of traders for mutual benefit
A business owned and controlled by a single family
A business wholly or partly owned and controlled by government
A business whose shares are traded only among friends
questions.e: A public enterprise is a business organisation that is wholly or partly owned, financed and controlled by government, set up to provide essential goods or services. Examples include statutory corporations and government-owned companies.
questions.p: Public enterprise na business wey government own full body or half-half to help provide important things for citizens. Examples na government corporations and companies wey government get hand inside.

questions.q: The management structure of a typical joint stock company includes shareholders, a board of directors, and management staff. Which of these correctly describes the relationship among them?
o: Shareholders elect directors who set policy, and management staff implement the policy
Directors and shareholders are the same group with identical duties
Management staff appoint directors who in turn appoint shareholders
Shareholders manage daily operations while directors only attend annual meetings
questions.e: In a joint stock company, shareholders who own the company elect a board of directors to formulate policy on their behalf, while employed management staff handle the day-to-day running of the business according to that policy. This separation of ownership and control is a defining feature of joint stock companies.
questions.p: For joint stock company, shareholders wey own the business go vote board of directors to make rules, and management staff go now run the work everyday. Dis one show say people wey own am dey different from people wey dey run am.

questions.q: A group of 40 civil servants in Lagos contributed money monthly, registered formally, and now use the pooled fund to grant each other low-interest loans and buy goods in bulk for resale to members at fair prices. This arrangement is best classified as a:
o: Cooperative society
Statutory corporation
Public limited liability company
Partnership business
questions.e: Pooling resources voluntarily for mutual benefit, such as granting loans and bulk buying for members, is the hallmark of a cooperative society. It is based on self-help and democratic member control rather than profit maximisation for outside investors.
questions.p: When people join hand save money, give themselves low-interest loan, and buy things join body for members, na cooperative society be that. E dey base on self-help and make life easy for members, no be just to make wicked gain.

questions.q: A key distinguishing feature of a statutory corporation, compared with a privately registered joint stock company, is that the statutory corporation is:
o: Owned entirely by foreign shareholders by law
Created directly by an Act of the National Assembly or a similar law
Registered under the Companies and Allied Matters Act like private firms
Required to distribute all its profit to private shareholders
questions.e: A statutory corporation is established by a specific Act of parliament or similar legislation, which defines its powers, functions and structure, unlike a joint stock company which is incorporated under general company law. This legal origin gives it a distinct status and often a monopoly in its area of operation.
questions.p: Na special Act of the National Assembly dem take dey create statutory corporation, unlike normal companies wey dem dey register under company law. Dis law wey create am na im dey give am im special power and duties.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of a short-term source of business finance?
o: Mortgage loan
Debenture
Ordinary share capital
Bank overdraft
questions.e: A bank overdraft is repayable within a short period, usually less than a year, making it a short-term source of finance. Debentures, shares and mortgages are long-term sources.
questions.p: Bank overdraft na short-term money wey person dey pay back quick quick, usually under one year. Na hin make am good short-term money source, unlike debenture and mortgage.

questions.q: Trade credit as a source of business finance means that a business is able to
o: receive a grant from government that does not require repayment
sell part of its ownership to the public through the stock exchange
obtain goods from suppliers now and pay for them at a later agreed date
borrow money from a commercial bank against fixed assets
questions.e: Trade credit allows a business to receive goods or services from a supplier immediately and pay later, which frees up cash for other uses. This is a common short-term source of finance for traders.
questions.p: Trade credit allow business make dem collect goods from supplier now and pay later. E dey help person free cash make e use do other business.

questions.q: Retained profit, as a source of finance, refers to the part of a company's profit that is
o: ploughed back into the business instead of being distributed
paid to government as company income tax
used to settle short-term creditors immediately
paid out to shareholders as dividend
questions.e: Retained profit is the portion of net profit that a business keeps and reinvests instead of distributing to owners as dividend. It is an internal, long-term source of finance that avoids interest payment.
questions.p: Retained profit na the money wey company keep inside business to use again instead of sharing am as dividend. E dey help business get money without paying interest.

questions.q: Alhaji Musa invested ₦500,000 as capital to start a poultry business. During the year, he introduced an additional ₦150,000 from his personal savings and withdrew ₦80,000 for family use. At the end of the year, his capital stood at ₦900,000. What was his profit for the year?
questions.e: Closing capital = Opening capital + Additional capital + Profit - Drawings. So Profit = 900,000 - 500,000 - 150,000 + 80,000 = 330,000. This is the standard capital reconciliation method.
questions.p: To find profit, we go add opening capital, additional capital and profit, then minus drawings to get closing capital. When we calculate am, the profit come be ₦330,000.

questions.q: A clothing store in Kano had an opening stock of ₦120,000, bought additional goods worth ₦480,000 during the month, and had a closing stock of ₦150,000. If the goods were sold at a uniform mark-up of 25% on cost, what was the turnover (sales) for the month?
questions.e: Cost of goods sold = Opening stock + Purchases - Closing stock = 120,000 + 480,000 - 150,000 = 450,000. With a 25% mark-up on cost, sales = 450,000 x 1.25 = 562,500.
questions.p: First, we go find cost of goods sold by adding opening stock and purchases, then minus closing stock to get ₦450,000. When we add the 25% mark-up on top, sales come be ₦562,500.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes an ordinary shareholder's position in a limited liability company?
o: A creditor entitled to a fixed rate of interest regardless of profit
A lender whose loan must be repaid before any dividend is paid to others
A part-owner of the company who bears the greatest risk but may enjoy higher returns
A government agent who regulates the company's financial activities
questions.e: Ordinary shareholders are owners of the company, not lenders, so they share in both the risks and the profits of the business. Unlike debenture holders, their returns depend on how well the company performs.
questions.p: Ordinary shareholders na the real owners of the company, and dem dey carry all the risk and profit. Dem money no get fixed interest like loan.

questions.q: A manufacturing company obtained a loan of ₦2,400,000 from a bank to be repaid over 8 years in equal annual instalments at a simple interest rate of 10% per annum on the original principal. What is the total amount the company will repay at the end of the loan period?
questions.e: Simple interest = Principal x Rate x Time = 2,400,000 x 10% x 8 = 1,920,000. Total repayment = Principal + Interest = 2,400,000 + 1,920,000 = 4,320,000.
questions.p: Simple interest for 8 years na ₦1,920,000. When you add am join the ₦2,400,000 principal, the total money wey company go repay na ₦4,320,000.

questions.q: Which of these is a major disadvantage of using retained profit as a source of business finance?
o: It reduces the amount available for distribution to owners as dividend
It attracts a high rate of interest that must be paid annually
It gives outsiders voting rights and control over the business
It must be repaid in full within one year of being used
questions.e: When a business keeps back part of its profit instead of paying it out, owners receive less dividend in the meantime. Unlike loans, retained profit does not attract interest and does not give outsiders control.
questions.p: When business use retained profit, owners no go get plenty money as dividend for that time. E good sha because e no get interest and outsiders no go control company.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes a 'bull' operator on the stock exchange?
o: An operator who sells securities he does not currently own, hoping to buy later at a lower price
An operator who trades only in government bonds and treasury bills
An operator who buys securities in anticipation of a price rise so as to sell later at a profit
An operator who buys securities only to hold permanently without reselling
questions.e: A bull is a speculator who expects prices to rise and buys shares now to sell later at a higher price. A bear does the opposite, selling now to buy back cheaper later.
questions.p: Bull na speculator wey dey expect say price go go up, na'im make 'e buy share now make 'e go sell am later for high price. Bear dey do opposite, 'e dey sell now make 'e come buy back cheap later.

questions.q: Treasury bills are best described as which type of security?
o: Long-term equity security issued by companies to raise permanent capital
Long-term government bond repayable after twenty years
Medium-term loan stock issued by companies and secured on fixed assets
Short-term government security used to finance temporary budget shortfalls
questions.e: Treasury bills are short-term debt instruments issued by government, usually maturing within a year, to meet short-term financing needs. They are not company equity or long-term bonds.
questions.p: Treasury bills na short-term debt instrument wey government dey issue, e dey usually mature within one year to support short-term money need. Dem no be company equity or long-term bond.

questions.q: Mr. Yakubu wants to invest in shares but has no idea which companies are financially sound. Which stock exchange functionary is trained to study company accounts and advise him on the best shares to buy?
o: Investment analyst
Issuing house
Jobber
Registrar
questions.e: An investment analyst studies company performance and market trends to give professional advice to investors. A jobber trades on his own account, while a registrar keeps shareholder records.
questions.p: Investment analyst dey check company performance and market trend to give better advice to people wey wan invest. Jobber dey trade for im own account, while registrar dey keep record of shareholder.

questions.q: Which of the following is a major function of the stock exchange in the Nigerian economy?
o: Granting short-term overdrafts to small businesses
Collecting company income tax on behalf of government
Providing a market for buying and selling of existing securities
Printing and issuing the national currency
questions.e: The stock exchange serves as a secondary market where existing shares and bonds already issued are bought and sold. It does not grant loans, print currency, or collect tax.
questions.p: Stock exchange dey act as secondary market where people dey buy and sell share and bond wey don already dey exist. E no dey give loan, print money, or collect tax.

questions.q: A preference shareholder in Okonma Plc is entitled to a fixed dividend before ordinary shareholders are paid, but has no voting right at the company's annual general meeting. This arrangement best illustrates which feature of preference shares?
o: Preference shares carry higher risk than ordinary shares
Preference shares combine a fixed return with limited control over company affairs
Preference shareholders rank below debenture holders but above ordinary shareholders in claims
Preference shares must always be redeemed within five years
questions.e: Preference shares typically give holders priority in dividend payment at a fixed rate, but in exchange they usually give up voting rights, unlike ordinary shareholders. This trade-off is their key feature.
questions.p: Preference share dey give holder priority to collect fixed dividend first, but dem no get voting right like ordinary shareholder. Na this trade-off make the feature special.

questions.q: A firm needs to raise fresh capital quickly without the expense of a full public offer, so it invites only a selected group of investors, such as pension funds and wealthy individuals, to subscribe for its new shares privately. This method of issuing shares is called
o: Offer by tender
Rights issue
Offer for sale
Private placement
questions.e: Private placement involves selling new shares directly to a select group of investors rather than to the general public, which is cheaper and faster than a public offer. This differs from a rights issue, which targets existing shareholders.
questions.p: Private placement mean say company dey sell new share directly to selected group of investor instead of general public, and e dey quick and cheap. E different from rights issue wey be say na existing shareholder dem target.

questions.q: Which of the following is a key requirement a company must usually satisfy before its shares can be listed on the Nigerian Stock Exchange?
o: The company must be owned entirely by foreign investors
The company must have a minimum level of share capital and a satisfactory profit record
The company must operate only in the manufacturing sector
The company must have fewer than ten employees
questions.e: Listing requirements generally demand that a company shows financial stability, adequate share capital, and a good profit track record to protect investors. Ownership by foreigners, sector type, or staff size are not listing conditions.
questions.p: Listing requirement mean say company must show say e get money stability, enough share capital, and good profit record to protect investor. Foreign ownership or small staff size no be condition for listing.

questions.q: Chambers of commerce in Nigeria usually organise trade fairs and exhibitions mainly in order to help member businesses to:
o: Avoid paying company income tax to the government
Fix uniform prices for all goods sold in the country
Display and promote their goods and services to a wider market
Obtain interest-free loans directly from the central bank
questions.e: Trade fairs and exhibitions give member firms a platform to showcase their products and services to potential customers, thereby widening their market. Chambers of commerce do not fix prices, grant tax waivers or give loans directly.
questions.p: Trade fairs dey give business people chance to show wetin dem dey sell to plenty customers. Dis one dey help dem market grow well well. Chambers of commerce no dey fix price or give loan.

questions.q: A consumer who buys a bag of rice from a shop in Onitsha discovers that the content weighs less than what is boldly written on the bag. Which consumer right has been violated in this situation?
o: The right to be heard
The right to choose freely among products
The right to accurate information about a product
The right to form a trade association
questions.e: The weight printed on the bag is information about the product, and giving false weight means the consumer was not given accurate information. The right to be heard concerns complaints, while forming a trade association is not a consumer right at all.
questions.p: If dem write weight for bag but di weight no reach, na lie dem dey lie. Consumer get right to know di correct truth about wetin e wan buy. Na why option C correct.

questions.q: One of the main objectives of forming a chamber of commerce in a town is to:
o: Represent the collective business interests of its members to government and other bodies
Replace the need for individual businesses to register with government agencies
Guarantee equal profit to every member business each year
Act as the sole importer of goods on behalf of its members
questions.e: A chamber of commerce speaks on behalf of the business community, presenting members' views and interests to government and other organisations. It does not replace legal registration requirements, guarantee profits, or act as a sole importer.
questions.p: Chamber of commerce na di voice of business people. Dem dey carry member matter go meet government so dat dem go fit help dem. Dem no dey guarantee profit or act as importer.

questions.q: A major reason why a consumer protection agency would investigate the labelling of a new brand of bottled drink before it is sold to the public is to ensure that the:
o: Manufacturer pays the correct import duty on raw materials
Product does not compete unfairly with other local drinks
Retail price is the same in every part of the country
Ingredients and expiry date are correctly and clearly stated
questions.e: Consumer protection bodies check labels mainly to confirm that ingredients, expiry dates and other safety information are correctly stated, so buyers are not misled or harmed. Import duty, competition issues and uniform pricing are not the main focus of labelling checks.
questions.p: Consumer protection agency must check label to make sure say expiry date and wetin dey inside drink dey clear. Dem dey do dis one so dat buyer no go drink poison. Label no concern import duty or price control.

questions.q: A group of furniture makers in Benin City form an association that sets minimum quality standards for members' products and also trains new entrants into the trade. This association is best described as performing which combination of functions?
o: Protecting members' interests and promoting professional standards within the trade
Collecting taxes from members on behalf of government
Acting as a court to settle all criminal cases involving members
Serving as the only bank through which members can save money
questions.e: Setting quality standards and training members are both ways a trade association protects its members' common interests and raises professional standards in the trade. Trade associations do not collect government taxes, act as criminal courts, or function as banks.
questions.p: When furniture makers join hand to set standard and train people, dem dey protect dia trade. Dis one dey help dem work better and keep professional standard. Association no be bank or court.

questions.q: A key difference between the role of a chamber of commerce and that of a government consumer protection agency is that the chamber of commerce mainly:
o: Sets the retail prices of goods nationwide, while the agency only advises on prices
Protects and promotes the interests of businesses, while the agency protects the interests of buyers
Issues licences to all businesses, while the agency only monitors advertising
Punishes businesses that sell substandard goods, while the agency has no such power
questions.e: A chamber of commerce exists chiefly to serve and advance the interests of its business members, whereas a consumer protection agency exists chiefly to safeguard the rights and welfare of consumers. The other statements wrongly describe the powers of either body.
questions.p: Chamber of commerce dey look after business people interest. Consumer protection agency dey look after buyer interest so dem no go cheat dem. Na two different work be dat.

questions.q: Marketing, as a business function, is best defined as the process of:
o: Recruiting and training staff to improve productivity
Keeping accurate records of all business transactions
Manufacturing goods in large quantities to reduce unit cost
Identifying, anticipating and satisfying customer needs profitably
questions.e: Marketing is the set of activities involved in identifying customer needs and satisfying them at a profit. The other options describe production, accounting and personnel management, not marketing.
questions.p: Marketing na how person go know wetin customer want and give dem wetin go make dem happy while you still make profit. Other things like making goods or keeping record no be marketing.

questions.q: Alhaji Musa owns a bakery in Kano. He first finds out what type of bread his customers prefer before baking and selling it, aiming to keep them loyal and satisfied. This approach shows that Alhaji Musa is practising the:
o: Marketing concept
Product concept
Selling concept
Production concept
questions.e: The marketing concept starts with identifying customer needs before producing goods to satisfy them. This is different from the production or selling concepts, which focus on output or aggressive selling without first studying customer wants.
questions.p: Marketing concept mean say you must first find out wetin customer want before you produce. Alhaji Musa dey follow dis rule because e dey ask wetin people want before e bake bread.

questions.q: A fashion designer in Lagos sets the price of her native attire by first considering what her target customers are willing and able to pay, rather than just adding a fixed profit margin to her cost. This pricing approach is best described as:
o: Cost-plus pricing
Break-even pricing
Customer-oriented pricing
Loss-leader pricing
questions.e: Customer-oriented pricing bases price decisions on what buyers perceive as fair value and can afford, reflecting the marketing concept. Cost-plus pricing instead starts from production cost plus a margin, which is not what the designer did.
questions.p: Customer-oriented pricing mean say you dey look wetin customer fit pay before you set price. The designer dey do dis one because e no just add profit on top cost, e dey consider the buyer.

questions.q: Which of the following best illustrates the 'place' element of the marketing mix for a company producing packaged cassava flour in Benue State?
o: Designing an attractive package with the company's logo
Running radio jingles to inform consumers about the flour's benefits
Offering a 10% discount during festive periods
Using distributors and supermarkets to make the flour available to consumers nationwide
questions.e: Place refers to the distribution channels and methods used to get a product from the producer to the final consumer. Packaging, discounts and radio jingles instead relate to product, price and promotion.
questions.p: Place for marketing mix na how you go take move goods from factory reach where customer go buy am. Using distributors and supermarkets na the correct way to make sure the flour reach everywhere.

questions.q: A soap manufacturer wants to launch a new brand targeted at young working-class women in urban Nigeria. To apply the marketing mix effectively, the company must ensure that decisions on product, price, place and promotion are:
o: Based solely on what competitors are doing
Coordinated and consistent with one another to support the same target market
Focused mainly on reducing production cost regardless of customer preference
Made independently by different departments without consultation
questions.e: The elements of the marketing mix must be blended together consistently so that the product, its price, where it is sold and how it is promoted all support the chosen target market. Treating them independently or copying competitors blindly can create a mismatched strategy that fails to meet customer needs.
questions.p: Marketing mix elements must work together like one body so that everything go align. If you no coordinate product, price, place and promotion, your business strategy no go fit work well.

questions.q: A company increases the amount spent on television adverts and employs more salesmen to visit retail shops and convince them to stock its new juice brand. These activities are best classified under which element of the marketing mix?
o: Product
Promotion
Place
Price
questions.e: Promotion covers all efforts to inform and persuade customers and retailers about a product, including advertising and personal selling by salesmen. It is distinct from product design, pricing decisions and distribution arrangements.
questions.p: Promotion na all the way wey you take dey tell people about your product so dem go buy. TV advert and using salesmen to convince shop owners na part of promotion.

questions.q: Two companies, X and Y, both sell bottled groundnut oil in Enugu at the same price and through the same supermarkets. Company X spends heavily on branding, quality packaging and after-sales service, while Company Y does none of these. Based on the marketing mix, Company X is most likely to gain an advantage mainly through superior:
o: Price strategy
Promotion budget alone
Product strategy
Place strategy
questions.e: Branding, packaging and after-sales service are features of the product element of the marketing mix, not price or place, since both companies are equal there. Since promotion is not mentioned as different, the advantage comes from a stronger overall product offering.
questions.p: Branding, packaging and after-sales service na part of product strategy. Since the price and place na the same for both companies, Company X dey win because their product get better value.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes the legal effect of 'revocation' of an offer under the law of contract?
o: The offeror withdraws the offer before it is accepted
The offeree rejects the offer outright
The offeror and offeree agree to cancel a signed contract
The offeree accepts the offer with new conditions
questions.e: Revocation occurs when the person who made the offer withdraws it before the other party has accepted. Once revoked, the offer can no longer be accepted to form a valid contract.
questions.p: Revocation mean say person wey make offer withdraw am before di other person accept am. Once dem revoke am, you no fit accept am again to form valid contract.

questions.q: Alhaji Musa bought a used tipper lorry from Garba Motors. Unknown to Alhaji Musa, the lorry had been reported as stolen before Garba Motors sold it to him. Under the Sale of Goods Law, which implied condition has been breached?
o: Condition as to merchantable quality
Condition as to sale by sample
Condition as to fitness for purpose
Condition as to title
questions.e: The law implies that a seller has the right to sell the goods and that the buyer will enjoy quiet possession. Since the lorry was stolen, Garba Motors had no good title to pass to Alhaji Musa.
questions.p: Law talk say seller must get right to sell wetin e dey sell. Because di lorry na stolen property, Garba Motors no get legal title to give Alhaji Musa.

questions.q: Which of the following is a duty that an agent owes to his principal under the law of agency?
o: To share equally in any loss suffered by the principal
To act within the scope of authority given and account for all monies received
To guarantee that the principal makes a profit from every transaction
To employ sub-agents without the principal's consent
questions.e: An agent must act within the authority granted and render a true account of all money or property received on the principal's behalf. The other options describe actions an agent is not required, or not permitted, to do.
questions.p: Agent must work according to wetin dem tell am do and e must show account for all money wey e collect for im principal. E no get duty to make profit or share loss.

questions.q: Bimpe agreed to buy a plot of land from Chief Ogunleye for N2,500,000, but the agreement was only spoken and never put in writing. Chief Ogunleye later refused to hand over the land. In relation to contracts concerning sale of land, what is the likely effect of this on Bimpe's ability to enforce the agreement in court?
o: The contract is fully enforceable because both parties agreed orally
The contract is void because land cannot be sold by agreement
The contract is generally unenforceable because contracts for sale of land must be evidenced in writing
The contract is voidable at the option of Bimpe only
questions.e: Contracts relating to the sale or transfer of interest in land fall under contracts that must generally be evidenced in writing (or by part performance) to be enforceable in court. Since there was no written evidence, Bimpe will find it difficult to enforce the oral agreement.
questions.p: Contract for land must dey for paper before court fit enforce am. Because Bimpe and Chief Ogunleye only talk am for mouth, e go hard for Bimpe to win for court.

questions.q: Under a hire purchase agreement, the hirer is best described as a person who
o: owns the goods immediately upon signing the agreement
transfers ownership of the goods to the owner at the end of the agreement
rents the goods permanently without any option to own them
pays by instalments and becomes owner only after paying the final instalment
questions.e: In a hire purchase agreement, the hirer uses the goods while paying instalments but only becomes the legal owner after the last instalment is paid along with any option-to-purchase fee. Before then, ownership remains with the owner/financier.
questions.p: For hire purchase, you dey pay small-small money to use di item. You go only become di real owner after you don pay di last instalment.

questions.q: Which of the following situations illustrates the termination of an agency relationship by 'operation of law' rather than by the acts of the parties themselves?
o: The principal dies suddenly, automatically ending the agent's authority
The agent completes the specific task for which he was appointed
The principal revokes the agent's authority in writing
The principal and agent mutually agree to end the arrangement
questions.e: Agency can end automatically by operation of law through events such as the death, insanity, or bankruptcy of either party, without any deliberate act by either side. The other options describe termination arising directly from the parties' own actions.
questions.p: Agency fit end by law if principal die, go mad, or go bankrupt. Dis one dey happen automatically without say any of dem plan am.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes the 'technological environment' as a component of the external business environment that a Nigerian soap manufacturer must monitor?
o: Changes in machinery, production methods and innovations that affect how goods are made and distributed
The amount of capital contributed by shareholders of the company
The rules guiding the internal promotion of staff within the firm
The level of literacy and age distribution of the workforce in the host community
questions.e: The technological environment covers advances in machinery, methods and innovations affecting production and distribution. The other options describe social, financial and internal management matters, not technology.
questions.p: Na technological environment dey cover machine advances, methods and innovations wey dey affect how goods dey made and distributed. Na only technology this one talk about, no be social, financial or internal management matter.

questions.q: A plastics company in Onitsha discovers that a new government regulation now requires all manufacturers to obtain an environmental compliance certificate before operating. This regulation belongs to which aspect of the business environment?
o: Economic environment
Socio-cultural environment
Political-legal environment
Demographic environment
questions.e: Government laws and regulations controlling business operations fall under the political-legal environment. It is not about income levels, culture or population structure.
questions.p: Government laws and regulations wey dey control business operations na under political-legal environment. E no get anything to do with income level, culture or population structure.

questions.q: Which of the following is the most accurate reason why business ethics is important to a firm's long-term survival?
o: It eliminates the need for the firm to pay company income tax
It guarantees that the firm will never make a loss
It allows the firm to ignore consumer protection laws legally
It helps build trust and a good reputation with customers, suppliers and regulators
questions.e: Ethical conduct builds trust and reputation, which encourages customer loyalty and smooth dealings with stakeholders. It does not remove tax obligations or guarantee profits.
questions.p: Ethical conduct dey help build trust and good reputation, wey come make customers loyal and business smooth with everybody. E no mean say company no go pay tax or say profit dey guaranteed.

questions.q: A beverage company in Ibadan is found to be under-declaring the sugar content on its product labels to appear healthier than competitors. This practice is best described as a violation of which area of business ethics?
o: Ethics in pricing policy
Ethics in advertising and product information
Ethics in employee welfare
Ethics in environmental conservation
questions.e: Misrepresenting product content on labels is a breach of honesty in advertising and product information. It has nothing to do with pricing, staff welfare or the environment directly.
questions.p: To dey lie about product content for label na breach of honesty for advertising and product information. E no concern pricing, staff welfare or environment directly.

questions.q: Which of the following actions by a company would be classified as discharging its ECONOMIC responsibility under corporate social responsibility, rather than its legal or philanthropic responsibility?
o: Complying with product safety standards set by regulators
Producing goods and services efficiently to earn profit and remain viable
Donating relief materials to flood victims
Obeying the minimum wage law set by government
questions.e: The economic responsibility is simply to produce goods profitably and remain a going concern. Obeying laws is a legal responsibility while donations are philanthropic responsibility.
questions.p: Economic responsibility na just to produce goods profitably and remain business going. To obey laws na legal responsibility, while gifts and donations na philanthropic responsibility.

questions.q: A cement factory in Benue consistently dumps untreated waste into a nearby river, harming fish farmers downstream, yet the factory pays its taxes and workers' salaries regularly. Which statement best evaluates the factory's conduct from a social responsibility standpoint?
o: The factory's conduct is acceptable because environmental matters are not part of social responsibility
The factory is fully socially responsible since it meets its legal and economic duties
The factory cannot be judged until it stops paying taxes
The factory is socially irresponsible because it neglects its responsibility to the environment and host community
questions.e: Meeting legal and economic duties alone does not make a firm socially responsible if it harms the environment and community; true social responsibility covers all stakeholders, including the environment. Paying tax and wages does not excuse pollution.
questions.p: Even if company dey pay tax and wages, to dey pollute environment and harm community mean say dem no socially responsible. True social responsibility cover everybody and everything, including nature.

questions.q: Which of the following best illustrates how a change in the ECONOMIC environment (such as a sharp rise in exchange rate) can directly affect a Nigerian company that imports raw materials?
o: The company's cost of production rises, forcing it to increase product prices or reduce output
The company is legally required to relocate its factory abroad
The company automatically becomes exempted from import duties
The company's workers gain an automatic right to form a trade union
questions.e: A rise in exchange rate makes imported raw materials more expensive in naira terms, raising production cost and often forcing price increases or output cuts. The other options are unrelated consequences of exchange rate changes.
questions.p: When exchange rate rise, imported raw materials go cost more money for naira, and this go increase production cost. E fit force company to increase price or reduce how much goods dem dey produce.

questions.q: A company's management argues that since shareholders bear all the financial risk, the firm's only responsibility is to maximise shareholder profit, with no duty to employees, consumers or the community. This view is most closely associated with which position on social responsibility?
o: The stakeholder theory of social responsibility
The triple bottom line approach to social responsibility
The traditional (classical) shareholder-only view of social responsibility
Carroll's four-part pyramid of social responsibility
questions.e: The classical or shareholder-only view holds that a firm's sole social responsibility is to maximise profit for its owners. Stakeholder theory, Carroll's pyramid and the triple bottom line all require broader responsibility to employees, consumers, community and environment.
questions.p: Na classical or shareholder-only view talk say company sole work na to make profit for owners. Other theories talk say company must care about workers, customers, community and environment.
